import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Badge } from './Badge' import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories' # Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar. ## Variants Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. | | `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. | | `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. | | `success` | As a dot, Online. | | `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. | `maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor. `isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/badge.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/badge](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/badge) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own is just the container. ## Measurements `md` is the xs control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Both sizes keep a single digit a circle: the minimum width equals the height. `sm` pads the count by 2px either side, below the spacing scale on purpose. A floating badge is centred on its corner of the anchor, half in and half out, with a 2px ring. ## Color A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour than their pill. ## States A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what it shows. }, { label: 'Over maxCount', content: }, { label: 'Zero', content: }, { label: 'Dot', content: }, ]} /> `count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean no badge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the anchor. ### Differences from the spec - **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on. The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking every consumer to position the anchor themselves. - **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue, which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background: the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour. - **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for presence and state dots. - **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification corner; the spec gives no default. - **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get mirrored placement. ## When to use Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar. A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on carries the meaning in its own name. } doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too." dont={} dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”." /> Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or a name beside it. ## When not to use - **For a label or category.** Use a [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words, a badge holds a number. - **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast. - **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything is, nothing stands out. ## Accessibility - An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12"). - A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside* the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead: `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`. - A **dot** has no text and is hidden too. - Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`. - Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

Above {children} Below
) # Divider A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items in a toolbar, blocks of a page. ## Variants | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. | | `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. | A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row. **Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as wide as its line. ## Measurements Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: the token layer has no border-width scale, and a rule should stay a crisp pixel at every `--scaling`. | Size | Thickness | | --- | --- | | `sm` | 1px | | `md` | 2px | | `lg` | 4px | ## Color Every size and appearance uses the same colour. ## States A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them apart. }, { label: 'Dashed', content: }, { label: 'Inset', content: }, { label: 'Decorative', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref` and `aria-hidden`. ### Differences from the spec - **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style. Solid versus dashed is a style. - **Thickness is raw px.** The token layer has no border-width scale, and a divider is the only component that needs three. ## When to use Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar. Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see. } doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning." dont={} dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group." /> ## When not to use - **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise. - **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space. - **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own border, not a Divider beside it. ## Accessibility - `
` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is already the default. - If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all. - The `--border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

Kbd is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental. ## Variants | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | Esc one key | A single key: `children`. | | combination | Keys pressed together: `keys`, one cap per key. | `size="sm"` (16px) fits inside a small control or a dense row; `md` (20px) is the default, for running text, tooltips and menus. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Kbd } from 'zweihander/kbd' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/kbd.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Kbd](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/kbd) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A combination is HTML's own markup for one: an outer `` holding a `` per key. A single key is just the cap. ## Measurements The border is 1px, 2px along the bottom so the cap reads as raised. ## Color ## States A key cap is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what it shows. ⌘ }, { label: 'Word', content: Esc }, { label: 'Combination', content: }, { label: 'sm', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the outer element. ## When to use Use Kbd wherever the page tells someone which key to press: a hint in a tooltip, a command palette row, a line of help text, a shortcuts sheet. These are places where people come to learn a shortcut, so the key gets a cap. A Menu is not: see below. } doCaption="Inside a control the caps are hidden and the button says Meta+K through aria-keyshortcuts: its name stays “Search”." dont={} dontCaption="Left in, the glyphs join the name: a screen reader hears “Search ⌘ K”, and ⌘ is read as “place of interest”." /> Match the platform: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Kbd shows what it is given and does not detect the platform. ## When not to use - **For a Menu item's shortcut.** Use Menu's `shortcut` string: menus show shortcuts as quiet text at the end of the row, the way desktop menus do. The menu is for acting, and a cap on every row would pull the eye from the labels. import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Tag } from './Tag' import * as TagStories from './Tag.stories' # Tag A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter chip, a person picked in a field. ## Variants `variant` is the colour: a status, or a hue for categories. `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | A plain label with no status: a type, a version. | | | Informational status: In review, Scheduled. The default. | | | Done or healthy: Paid, Verified, Live. | | | Needs attention soon: Expiring, Pending. | | | Failed or blocked: Overdue, Error. | | | A hue: one per category, label or owner. It carries no meaning. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | | Most places: a tint that sits in a row of text. | | | Dense tables and busy surfaces, where many tints would be loud. | | | One tag that must stand out: a single status on a card. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tag } from 'zweihander/tag' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tag.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tag](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tag) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy ## Measurements A tag sits in a line of text, so each size reads the control tier below its name (Foundations / Sizing): `md` is tier sm, `sm` is tier xs. A 1px padding and a 1px border, transparent unless outlined, make up the tier's height, so appearances never shift the layout. The corner follows the Theme's radius preset like every control: a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`. ## Color Each variant has a solid, a colour on that solid, a subtle tint and a text colour that subtle and outlined use. Subtle and outlined text is measured at 4.5:1 by the token build. Every hue follows the same four tokens under its own name. Red, as an example; the other sixteen swap `red` for their hue. ## States The tag itself is not interactive. Its remove button is: - **Hover** tints the button with the tag's own text colour at 15%, so it reads on every variant and appearance without a token for each. - **Focus** is the `--ring` outline every control uses, drawn inset so it stays inside a 20px tag. - Pressing removes nothing by itself: `onRemove` reports it, and the parent drops the tag from its list. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the container, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **The spec's four variants needed new tokens.** `info`, `success`, `warning` and `danger` were added to the token layer for Tag and are shared with Alert and Toast. - **No `isRounded`.** The corner reads the control tier's radius, so it follows the Theme's radius preset with every other control, and turns into a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`. - **The 17 hue variants are additions.** Solid is step 600 with a white label on every hue, in both appearances, so a row of solid tags reads as one set; on the warm hues (orange, amber, yellow, lime and others) that label falls below 4.5:1. That is accepted on purpose. - **`startAvatar` wins over `startIcon`** if both are passed; the spec does not say. - **The tag does not remove itself.** `onRemove` reports the click and the parent drops the tag from its list, so the list stays the one source of truth. ## When to use Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1. } doCaption="Warm hues in subtle: every label clears 4.5:1." dont={} dontCaption="The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1." /> Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says what the status is. In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6` between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 10px above and below a 24px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap. ## When not to use - **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). - **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a Checkbox. - **For a count.** Use a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs). ## Accessibility - The remove button is named **"Remove `text`"** (e.g. "Remove Design"), so a list of tags does not read as a row of identical "Remove" buttons. - It is a native `

One per view. | | | A strong action in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | | Everything else: Cancel, Back, Export. | | | Deleting, or anything that cannot be undone. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The action to take, filled so it is found first. | | | Actions that matter but are not the next step. | | | Low emphasis and dense places: toolbars, table rows, a card's corner. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Button } from 'zweihander/button' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button.json ``` - Source: [src/components/buttons/Button.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/Button.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/button](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/button) - Behaviour: [Base UI Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy While `isLoading`, a spinner takes the content's place; the content stays, invisible, so the button keeps its width and its name. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Buttons take the spacious inline padding: a centred label needs more room either side than a field's left-aligned text. An icon-only button is square: its width is its height. With `isFullWidth` it fills its container. ## Color Each variant has a solid (the contained fill), a colour on that solid, and a tone that outlined and ghost use for their label. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. Ghost and outlined have no fill at rest. Contained is lit from above: a lighter top, a highlight on the top edge, a darker bottom edge and a hairline border a step darker than the solid. Each is the variant's solid moved in lightness, so it has no token of its own and follows the accent and the mode. ## States }, { label: 'Loading', content: }, ]} > - **Hover and pressed** are mixed from the variant's own colours, not a token each. A coloured solid (primary, destructive) moves away from its label and gains contrast; accent and secondary move toward it. Outlined and ghost tint the background with their tone, 8% on hover and 14% when pressed. Every state keeps the label at 4.5:1, measured by the `StateContrast` story under all seventeen accents in both modes. - **Hover**, on contained, also draws a 1px hairline ring standing `--focus-offset` off the button, where the focus ring sits, so focus replaces it rather than adding a second ring. Inside a ButtonGroup the ring is left out: it would cut across the next button. - **Pressed**, on contained, turns the light over: shade on the top edge, no drop shadow, no gradient, as if pushed in. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the button. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity. - **Loading** keeps the full colour: the button is busy, not unavailable. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox' import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories' # Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked, indeterminate. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. | | | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. | **Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never "mixed". ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The box is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label wraps to. The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio. ## Color ## States }, { label: 'Indeterminate', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to `--foreground`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the box. - **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%. - **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box. ### Differences from the spec - **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange` for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms. - **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property, not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI calls it `indeterminate`. - **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a focusable ``, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship. ## When to use Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens until the form is sent. Write the label so that checked means yes. } doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes." dont={} dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out." /> ## When not to use - **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit. - **For one choice out of several.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes are independent. - **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate. Space toggles it. - The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box. - `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets `aria-invalid`. - The unchecked outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page on every gray ramp. - A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form submission and validation. - 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers, without the box growing.

components-controls-color-picker--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker' import * as ColorPickerStories from './ColorPicker.stories' # Color Picker Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a saturation and brightness area and a hue strip, or type its channels in Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB. The panel is laid out like Figma's colour picker. ## Variants Two exports. | Export | Use for | | --- | --- | | `ColorPicker` | A form field: the hex in a text field, with a swatch button that opens the panel in a popover. | | `ColorPanel` | The panel on its own, always open: a sidebar, an inspector, a settings page about colour. | `alpha` adds opacity; `defaultFormat` picks which channels the fields show first. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ColorPicker, ColorPanel } from 'zweihander/color-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/color-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/color-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/color-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The panel here is shown open under its field; in a `ColorPicker` it opens in a popover from the swatch button. ## Measurements The field is a Text Input: the same tiers, padding and label. The panel is the same at both field sizes. The panel is 16rem wide, so eight swatches fit in a row, and the area is 10rem tall. The format menu and the channels are the kit's md (32px) Select and field box. ## Color The area, the hue strip and the checkerboard are the colour model itself, so they are fixed colours, not theme tokens. The thumbs are white rings with a dark edge: one of the two is at least 3:1 against whatever colour is under them. Swatches have a faint inner edge, black 10% in light mode and white 10% in dark, as in Figma. That is below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 round a white swatch on white, accepted because the hex in the field, not the edge, tells the colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** follows Text Input on the field. In the panel every thumb, swatch and field draws a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside. - **Disabled** dims the field and disables the swatch button. - **Error** is Text Input's. Typed text that is not a colour turns the field to error on its own, with a hint, and keeps the last good value. - **Chosen swatch** has a 2px `--primary` ring; focused as well, the ring turns `--ring` and moves 1px further out. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ColorPanel` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `alpha`, `defaultFormat`, `swatches`, `disabled` and `className`. `parseColor(text)` reads any CSS colour (`rgb(59 130 246)`, `hsl(217 91% 60% / 50%)`, `oklch(...)`, `rebeccapurple`) to the same hex, or `null`; the browser parses it, so outside one only hex is read. `normalizeHex(text)` turns `#abc`, `ABC` or `#AABBCC` into `#aabbcc`, keeps an alpha byte (`#3b82f680`, or `#abc8` as `#aabbcc88`) unless it is `ff`, and turns anything else into `null`. ### Design notes - **Hex in, hex out.** The value is lowercase `#rrggbb`, with an alpha byte only while opacity is under 100%. Typed text is read on Enter or blur: hex of 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits with or without `#`, or any CSS colour. It is shown back as hex. - **Formats are a view, not a value.** RGB, HSL and HSB only change the fields; the value stays hex. Channel fields commit on Enter or blur, and up and down step by 1 (Shift by 10), as in a design tool. - **The hue is remembered.** The picker keeps hue, saturation and brightness, so dragging to black and back leaves the hue strip where it was instead of jumping to red. - **Not in this version:** Figma's library picker ("On this page"), gradients and an eyedropper. ## When to use Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow, offer it as named swatches. } doCaption="The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex." dont={} dontCaption="A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off." /> ## When not to use - **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag colours, a theme accent), use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour. - **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text. ## Accessibility - The field is a text input named by its label. The swatch button is named "Choose colour, #3b82f6 selected", and the popover is a dialog named "Choose colour" that returns focus to the button on Escape. - The area is one tab stop: a slider named "Saturation" whose value text reads both numbers ("Saturation 76%, brightness 96%"). Left and right change saturation, up and down brightness, Shift moves 10%, Page Up and Page Down change brightness by 10%, Home and End set saturation to 0 or 100%. A second "Brightness" slider is there for a screen reader's browse mode. - The hue strip is a slider named "Hue", read as "217 degrees"; the opacity strip, "Opacity", read as "50%". - The format menu is the kit's Select, named "Colour format". Channel fields are text inputs named for what they hold ("Red", "Hue degrees", "Lightness percent", "Opacity percent", "Hex"), so they do not share a name with the sliders. - Swatches are native radios in a radio group named "Swatches": one tab stop, arrows move and choose, and the chosen one is checked. None is checked while the colour is not one of them. They are 24px with 8px between them, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 without a larger invisible target. - A colour is never the only way to know the value: the hex is always in the field.

The selected radio is the foreground colour. | | `primary` | A choice that carries the brand: a plan picker beside a primary button. | | Orientation | Use for | | --- | --- | | `vertical` | The default. Options with helper text, or labels longer than a word or two. | | `horizontal` | Two to four short labels: sizes, yes or no. The row wraps when narrow. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/radio.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Radio.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Radio.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio) - Behaviour: [Base UI Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio), [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and [Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each option's label wraps its radio, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The circle is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits centred on the first line of its label. The legend is the body size at medium weight. ## Color An option's own helper describes the option, so it stays muted when the group is in error or success; only the group message takes that colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on an option's label darkens an unselected ring to `--foreground`. `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the group. ### Differences from the spec - **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props" convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components. - **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's `value` says which is checked. - Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox. ## When to use Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one. } doCaption="A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected." dont={} dontCaption="Ten radios are a wall to scan. A long list belongs in a Select or a Combobox." /> ## When not to use - **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on screen.** Use a Select, or a Combobox when the reader knows what to type. - **For several choices at once.** Use [Checkboxes](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs). - **For a single on or off.** Use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) in a form, or a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs) for a setting that applies at once. ## Accessibility - A `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Calendar } from './Calendar' import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories' # Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs). ## Variants Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. | | A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. | | Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. | | Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. | | Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. | The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US` on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar) - Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them. Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange disc, round where a selected day takes the control's corners; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day, behind the days between the two ends. The band rounds off where a week or the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded, so two months side by side never draw the same day twice. ## Measurements Calendar has one size. Days are 32px, 4px apart: each cell pads by half of `--space-1` on every side, so a range's band runs unbroken under the gap. Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px, the touch target; the previous and next buttons stay 32px. ## Color One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - **Day** has no fill at rest. - **Today's figure is dark**, not white: white on `--orange` is 3.4:1, under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure needs, while `--orange-contrast` clears 4.9:1 in both modes. A selected today shows as selected. - **Outside days** are `--muted-foreground` mixed 50% with transparent, about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked. - **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not rely on colour. ## States }, { label: 'Today', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--accent` behind `--accent-foreground`. The selected day and today keep their own colours; unavailable and outside days do not react. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the day. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the selected look follows. - **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons disable at the limits, at 50% opacity. - **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is the orange disc, round. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are banded. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange` type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored. ## When to use Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than refusing the choice after it is made. } doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them." dont={} dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker." /> Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28 February, not 3 March. ## When not to use - **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs): it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted. - **For a span inside a form.** Use a [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs): it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here. - **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content. Use the [Event Calendar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--docs) pattern, or list the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs). ## Accessibility - A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`. - Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September 2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`. - One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected. - Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the next one. - Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day) and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored. - The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced. - The previous and next buttons are named "Previous month" and "Next month", and are disabled at `min` and `max`. - Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Every appearance takes every size and orientation. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `elevated` | The default panel: a white `--card` on the off-white page, with an edge and a faint shadow. | | `outline` | Cards in a dense grid or inside another panel, where a shadow per card is too much. | | `unstyled` | The card's padding and layout with nothing visible, e.g. inside a surface that already has its own. | | `surface` | A block of an AppShell page. It follows the Theme's `contentStyle`: raised like `elevated` when the content is `card`, a section set off by a rule above when it is `flat`. See [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs). | `size` sets the padding and the gap between children, from 12px (`xs`) to 32px (`lg`). `orientation="horizontal"` sets the children side by side: media, text and an action. With `onClick` the whole card is one button; with `render={}` it is a link. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Card } from 'zweihander/card' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Card.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Card.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/card](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/card) - Composition: [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The card is only the container. Title and body are your own elements, at the heading level the page needs. ## Measurements Each size is a step of the spacing scale, padding on every side and the gap between children. The border is 1px, transparent when `hasBorder` is off, so turning it on or off never moves the content. `isRounded={false}` gives square corners. ## Color Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. `unstyled` has no background, border or shadow, and its content takes the colour of what it sits on. `surface` takes `elevated`'s colours under `contentStyle="card"`. Under `contentStyle="flat"` it has no background, radius or shadow, only `--border` along its top edge. ## States A plain card is a container and has no states. A clickable or link card has these: }, ]} > - **Hover** never touches the surface: muted text sits on `--card` at 4.5:1 with no margin to spare, and darkening it 6% took muted text to 3.9:1. An `elevated` card lifts to `--shadow-md`; an `outline` card's edge strengthens to `--control-border`, the 3:1 control border. An `unstyled` card has no hover look. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the card. - **Pressed and disabled** have no look of their own. A card has no `disabled` prop: a card that cannot act is a plain card. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **`children`, not `content`.** Arbitrary content is what React children are for. - **`orientation` defaults to `vertical`.** The spec says `horizontal`, which would lay a title and its description side by side. - **`render` is added** so a card can be a link, alongside `onClick` for a card that acts. - **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's tinted card was dropped to match the Claude apps, where a panel is a white `--card` on the off-white page, with an edge or a faint shadow. - **`unstyled`** keeps the padding and layout and drops every visual. ## When to use Use a Card to group content about one thing, so it reads as a unit: a person, a plan, a setting. Put headings inside at the level the page needs; the card has none of its own. A clickable card is one button, and a button may only hold phrasing content: use spans for its title and text, not headings or paragraphs, and put no links or buttons inside it. If a card needs its own actions, leave it plain and put a button in it. } doCaption="A plain card with its own Follow button: each control is reachable on its own." dont={} dontCaption="A button inside a clickable card is invalid HTML, and neither control can be reached reliably." /> A card that navigates should be a link (`render={}`), not a button with a click handler: a link opens in a new tab and shows its address. ## When not to use - **For rows of data to compare.** Use a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): columns line values up, cards do not. - **To show and hide content.** Use an [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs) or a [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs). - **Just to add space or a background.** A plain `
` with padding does that without suggesting a unit. ## Accessibility - A plain card is a `
`: no role, no tab stop, nothing added to the accessibility tree. - **A clickable card is one `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as CarouselStories from './Carousel.stories' # Carousel A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery, onboarding cards. ## Variants The carousel has no `variant` prop. These are its configurations: | Configuration | Use for | | --- | --- | | One in view (default) | Large slides that each need the full width: a feature, a photo. | | `slidesPerView={3}` | Smaller items browsed in a row: templates, products. | | `loop` | A short set with no natural first or last, where next from the end should wrap. | | `autoPlay` | Rarely. A showcase where motion is the point; it adds a stop/start button. | With three in view, five slides have three stops (1-3, 2-4, 3-5), and the dots count stops, not slides. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Carousel } from 'zweihander/carousel' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/carousel.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/carousel](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/carousel) - Behaviour: [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The controls sit above the track, at its end, so they never cover a slide. A visually hidden line after the track says where the reader is (see Accessibility). - **Native scrolling.** No transform maths and no gesture library: the track is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch, trackpad and momentum behave as the platform does. The index is read back once the track comes to rest. - **Right to left works.** Offsets are measured from the first slide, so the negative `scrollLeft` of a right-to-left track reads correctly, and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored. - **`defaultIndex` starts there.** The track jumps to it on mount, without a scroll animation. ## Measurements There is one size. Slide width follows from the carousel's width, `slidesPerView` and the gap between slides. A dot is 6px round (1.5 × `--space-1`); the current one stretches to a 24px pill. Buttons have a 1px border. ## Color The carousel has no variants: one table. Slides bring their own colours. ## States }, { label: 'Last stop', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** fills an enabled button with `--accent` and its icon with `--accent-foreground`. Dots have no hover look. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the track, a button or a dot. - **Pressed** has no look of its own. - **Disabled**: previous at the first stop and next at the last, unless `loop`. A disabled button is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with the disabled cursor and no hover. - **Current slide**: the current stop's dot is the longer `--foreground` pill. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Everything in a carousel past the first slide is hidden until the reader goes looking. Use one for content that is fine to miss: featured items, examples, a gallery. Give it a `label` that names what is in it. } doCaption="Featured templates: browsing is optional, and missing one costs nothing." dont={} dontCaption="Account notices the reader must act on, four of them hidden in slides most readers never reach." /> Prefer no `autoPlay`. Motion pulls the eye away from the rest of the page, and a slide can move on before it has been read. ## When not to use - **For content everyone must see.** Show it at once: a list, or [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) in a grid, show more and hide nothing. - **For items to compare.** Use a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): side by side beats one at a time. - **For steps in a flow.** Use a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it shows how many steps there are and where you are. ## Accessibility Follows the [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/). - A `
` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and your `label`; each slide is a group with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and a name like "2 of 5". - Previous, next, stop/start and the dots are native buttons: Tab reaches them, Enter and Space press them. - Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. Dots are buttons named "Slide 3", with `aria-current` on the current stop. - **Autoplay** (WCAG 2.2.2) pauses while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside it, has a stop/start button as its first control, and never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`. - A visually hidden line says where you are ("Slide 3 of 5", or "Slides 3 to 5 of 5"). It is `aria-live="polite"` when the reader moves the carousel, so a screen reader hears the change, and `off` while it rotates on its own. Every slide is in the DOM from the start, so a live region round the track would stay silent. - The track is in the tab order (`tabindex="0"`), like any scrolling region. - In right to left, the previous and next chevrons are mirrored. - Buttons and dots have 44px touch targets on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ColumnChooserStories from './ColumnChooser.stories' # Column Chooser A button above a table that opens a list of its columns, each with a checkbox to show or hide it, and a Reset that brings back the default set. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Every column shown (default) | Tables whose columns all matter at first, where people hide what they do not need. | | `defaultVisibleKeys` | Tables with more columns than fit: show the essentials, let people add the rest. Reset goes back to this set. | The chooser does not touch the table: it reports the shown keys and you filter the Table's `columns` with them. That keeps the choice yours to store, per user or per view. With a resizable Table, pass `onReset` to put the widths back too: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ColumnChooser } from 'zweihander/column-chooser' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/column-chooser.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; built from the Application UI catalogue, whose source for widths is shadcn's Resizable. Widths are Table's `isResizable` instead, a handle in each header rather than resizable panels - Behaviour: the kit's [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) and [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real choosers rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the button where it opens. ## Measurements The button is a medium Button and Reset a small one; the popover, its padding and title are Popover's. Checkboxes keep their own sizes. ## Color The chooser adds no colour of its own: the button is an outlined secondary Button, Reset a ghost secondary Button, and the surface is Popover's `--popover`. See those pages for their tokens. ## States The chooser is open or closed. The button keeps Button's states; each box keeps Checkbox's, and a locked column shows Checkbox's disabled look: - **Locked**: the row header column, and the last column left, are ticked and disabled: a table needs a name per row and at least one column. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Differences from the spec There is no uiguideline spec. The catalogue's anatomy lists drag to reorder as optional; it is left out until a table needs it, because it needs a keyboard way to move as well. ## When to use Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones. } doCaption="A few optional columns beside a locked name column." dont={} dontCaption="A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose." /> ## When not to use - **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once. - **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in the table's toolbar. - **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is used on, leave them all shown. ## Accessibility - The button reports `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by the label, "Columns". - Opening moves focus into the dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button. - Each column is a checkbox named by its header, in table order; Space toggles it, and the shown keys are reported in column order, the row header always among them. - The row header column's checkbox, and the last checked one, are `aria-disabled`: ticked and unchangeable. - Reset is a button named "Reset" that brings back the default columns.

components-data-display-resizable--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Resizable } from './Resizable' import * as ResizableStories from './Resizable.stories' # Resizable Two panes split by a handle that people drag, or move with the arrow keys, to give one pane more room: a list beside its detail, a query above its results. Resizable is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental. ## Variants | Orientation | Use for | | --- | --- | | `horizontal` (default) | Panes side by side: a list and the record picked from it, a file tree and the file. | | `vertical` | Panes stacked: an editor over its output, a chart over its table. | `minSize` and `maxSize` keep the first pane between two sizes, in percent of the whole, so neither pane can be dragged out of sight. For three panes, put a Resizable in a pane of another. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Resizable } from 'zweihander/resizable' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/resizable.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx) - Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Resizable](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/resizable) and the [APG window splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) - Base UI: none; Base UI has no splitter - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The limits, `minSize` and `maxSize`, have no element of their own: they are where the handle stops. ## Measurements The line is 1px; its hit area reaches past it on both sides, and grows to 44px on touch screens without the line getting wider. The panes have no padding of their own: what goes in them sets it. Sizes are percentages of the whole, so the split holds when the window changes size. ## Color ## States
- **Hover** and **Dragging** thicken the line to 2px `--primary`, as on Table's column resize handle. The cursor turns to a resize arrow. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the line. - There is no disabled state: a split that should not move is two plain boxes. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Resizable fills its parent: give the parent a height for side-by-side panes, and both a height for stacked ones. ### Differences from the spec shadcn's Resizable is a group of any number of panels and handles (`ResizablePanelGroup`, `ResizablePanel`, `ResizableHandle`). Zweihänder takes flat props and two panes, `start` and `end`, as its API conventions ask; nest one for three panes. There is no collapse on Enter and no saved layout: store `onSizeChange` to keep the split. ## When to use Use Resizable where people need to trade room between two things they look at together, and the right split depends on the content: a long name in a list, a wide table in the detail. } doCaption="Each handle is named after the pane it sizes: “Resize folders”, “Resize inbox”." dont={} dontCaption="Both handles keep the default name, so a screen reader hears “Resize” twice and cannot tell them apart." /> Keep `minSize` above zero (the default is 10%), so a pane cannot be dragged out of sight with its content still in the tab order. ## When not to use - **For a fixed sidebar beside the page.** Use the App Shell template: its Nav Sidebar has a set width and collapses. - **For a panel that slides over the page.** Use Drawer. - **For a column of a table.** Use Table's `isResizable`. - **For layouts that only change with the window.** Use the Multi-column layout template: Resizable is for people, not breakpoints. ## Accessibility - The handle is a focusable `role="separator"`, after the APG window splitter. Side by side it is `aria-orientation="vertical"`; stacked it is `"horizontal"`. - Its name is `handleLabel` and `aria-controls` points at the first pane. - `aria-valuenow` is the first pane's size in percent, between `aria-valuemin` (`minSize`) and `aria-valuemax` (`maxSize`). - Side by side, Arrow Right moves the handle 16px right and Arrow Left 16px left; in right-to-left text the first pane is on the right, so Arrow Left grows it. Stacked, Arrow Down and Arrow Up do the same. Home moves it to `minSize`, End to `maxSize`. These are the keys and the step of Table's column resize handle. - Dragging the handle moves it by the distance dragged, never past the limits.

components-data-display-table--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TableStories from './Table.stories' # Table Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects, invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected, expanded and acted on, and a total row can sum them up. ## Variants Any table takes any of these together: a selectable table can also expand its rows and keep its header in view. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `density="md"` | The default, 48px rows: most tables, and rows that hold a Tag or a button. | | `density="sm"` | 40px rows, for long lists of plain text where seeing more rows at once matters. | | `isSelectable` | Acting on several rows at once: archive, export, assign. | | `expandedContent` | Details that belong to one row but do not fit in a column: a description, a timeline, line items. | | `hasStickyHeader` | Long tables that scroll inside a fixed height, so the column names stay in view. | | `rowActions` | Actions on one record (edit, duplicate, archive) that do not earn a column: a menu at the row's end. | | `footer` on a column | A total row under the rows: sums, counts, averages. | | `isResizable` | Tables whose columns hold text of unknown length (names, notes, emails), so people can widen what they read. | | `emptyState` | Saying why there are no rows, and what to do: clear a search, add the first one. | Rows with details open under themselves. Expansion is independent of selection and survives sorting: A menu at the end of each row. A row with nothing to do gets no button: `hasRowContextMenu` also opens a row's `rowActions` at the pointer on right click or long press, through [Context Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-context-menu--docs), as Stacked List and Grid List do. It is off by default: the row then loses the browser's own menu, so people can no longer copy a cell's text or open a link in a cell in a new tab from it. Turn it on for tables people work through record by record, not ones they read or copy from. A row with no items, and an expanded row's details, keep the browser's menu. A total row under the rows, which sorting leaves at the bottom. The table does not add anything up: you pass each column's `footer`, so you decide whether it totals this page or every row. A handle on each header's end edge resizes its column, by dragging or by the arrow keys. The table is then laid out by its header widths: give the columns a starting `width`, and keep `columnWidths` if they should last. Pair it with a [Column Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs) to hide columns as well. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Table, type TableColumn } from 'zweihander/table' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Table.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Table.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table) - Behaviour: a native ``; selection uses the kit's [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs), expansion its [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs), row actions its [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The table sits in a container that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen rather than squeezing the columns. The selection column comes first, then the expand column; the actions column comes last. A row whose `expandedContent` or `rowActions` returns nothing leaves that cell empty. The total row is a ``, so it stays at the bottom whatever the sort. ## Measurements Each density is a row height. Everything else is the same in both. The handle line is 1px at rest, like the row dividers; no token covers a hairline. Its strip is 16px wide (44px on touch screens), at the header's end, over the header's own padding. A column is 48px to 1200px wide; the arrow keys move it 16px at a time. Rows are divided by a 1px rule; the last row has none. The sort button pulls itself out by its own inline padding, so its label lines up with the cells below. Figures are tabular, so numbers line up column-wide. ## Color Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - Rows are not striped: the dividers separate them. - The sort icon of a column that is not sorted is the label's colour at 60% opacity. - **Between two selected rows** the divider is mixed from the tint: `--primary-subtle` with a quarter of `--primary-subtle-text`. `--border` is as light as the tint in light mode and would vanish. - **An open row and its content read as one block**: no divider between them, and the content row shares its row's hover and selected tint. ## States }, { label: 'Selected', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every row and button at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** tints the row with `--accent`, and the sort button too. The content row of an open row takes no hover of its own, only its row's. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, drawn 2px inside the sort button. The checkboxes and the expand button keep their own focus rings. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click sorts, selects or opens, and that state's look follows. - **Resize handle**: hover and drag thicken its line to 2px `--primary`; focus draws the `--ring` outline inside the handle. - **Disabled**: Table has none. A row that cannot be acted on is a row without the control. - **Sorted** shows the column's icon at full colour, pointing up or down. - **Selected** tints the row with `--primary-subtle`. - **Expanded** turns the chevron to point down and opens the content row under it. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TableColumn` describes one column: - `key`: unique; also the row field shown when there is no `cell`. - `header`: the column's label. - `cell`: renders the cell; defaults to `row[key]`. - `sortable`: adds a sort button to the header. It sorts by `sortValue`, or by `row[key]`. - `align`: `start`, `center` or `end`. `end` for numbers and dates, so the digits line up. - `width`: any CSS width, e.g. `8rem` or `20%`. - `isRowHeader`: makes the column's cells `
`, the name a row is known by. Usually the first column. - `footer`: this column's cell in the total row, e.g. a sum. Any column with one adds the row; put the label ("Total") on the row header column. Hidden while there are no rows. `TableSort` is `{ key, direction }`, with direction `ascending` or `descending`. With `sort` controlled, the table leaves the order to you. `sortRows(rows, columns, sort)` returns the rows in the order the table would sort them, so you can sort every row before slicing out a page, as the [Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs) template does. ## When to use Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`. } doCaption="Numbers and dates aligned to the end, in tabular figures: the digits line up column-wide." dont={} dontCaption="Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance." /> } doCaption="A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”." dont={} dontCaption="Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select." /> **Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled, the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways. With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the rows already sorted: **Paging is not built in.** Put a [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only. Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table: ## When not to use - **For a whole list page** with search, filters, bulk actions and paging. Start from the [Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs) pattern, which puts a Table together with them. - **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs). - **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader; use CSS grid to place things side by side. - **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit has no data grid yet. ## Accessibility - A real `` named by its `` with one cell per column, so each total is announced under its column; the label column is its row header.
`, with `
` headers and a `` for the row header column: screen readers announce the column and the row for every cell. - Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header. - Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`. - Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"), reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state. - A row with nothing to expand has no button. - The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column is announced like the others. - The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its row. - Each row actions button is named after the row header ("Actions for Atlas") and reports `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Enter opens the menu, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. A row with no items has no button. - The actions column's header is "Actions", visually hidden. - With `hasRowContextMenu`, the right-click menu is a shortcut to the same entries, never the only way in: the ⋯ button stays. - When the table is wider than its box and nothing in it takes focus, the scroll box becomes a tab stop with a focus ring: `role="region"` named by the caption, which the browser scrolls with the arrow keys. A table that fits, or whose cells hold a control (a sort button, a checkbox), gets no extra tab stop. - With `isResizable`, each column header holds a focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Resize" and the header ("Resize Owner"), or the column's `key` when the header is not plain text. Its `aria-valuenow` is the column's width in px, between `aria-valuemin` 48 and `aria-valuemax` 1200. - Arrow Right widens the column 16px and Arrow Left narrows it (mirrored in right-to-left); Home sets the narrowest width and End the widest. {children}
) # Combobox A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one. ## Variants Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and marks the match; the chosen option carries a check. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Forms and settings: the default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row, beside `sm` buttons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it: - **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and underline. Options are inset by the field's padding, so their text starts where the input's does. - **Check**: before the chosen option's label, in a column kept for every option so labels never shift. - **Message**: "No matches" (`emptyText`) when nothing matches, "Loading…" while `isLoading`. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Fields take the normal inline padding, so the value lines up with the label above it, and the field radius, which never becomes a pill. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; the list is at least as wide as the field, 4px under it, and scrolls after 20rem (about ten options). ## Color The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1, as in the Claude apps: an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11. The label, placeholder and focus ring still mark the field. The matched text keeps the option's own colour, so it holds full contrast on the highlighted row. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Loading', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while the input has focus, by pointer too: that is where typing goes. In the error state the ring is `--danger-text`. The clear and open buttons draw their own ring when tabbed to, so the field never shows two. - **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the clear and open buttons darken from `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`. - **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text` together; the words are the message, the colour only points at it. - **Read-only** fills the field with `--surface-filled`; there is no clear button. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity. - **Loading** adds a spinner before the buttons and says "Loading…" in the list. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Differences from the spec - **Labels must be strings**, not components: they are what is typed, matched and shown in the input. - **`emptyText`** is added: an empty list needs to say why. - **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, and native names (`disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`), as on Select. ## When to use Use a Combobox to choose one option from a long list, when people already know what they are looking for: a person, a country, a project. Typing a few letters is faster than scrolling. It chooses from the list only; free text that is not an option is not a value. } doCaption="A long list people know an entry of: type a few letters, pick it." dont={} dontCaption="Three options hidden behind typing. A Select or a radio group shows them all." /> ## When not to use - **For a handful of options.** Under about seven, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group when they should all be visible. - **For free text.** If any answer is valid, use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs); to filter a page, use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs). - **For several values.** It holds one; a multi-select is not built yet. ## Accessibility - The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` named by the field's label (or `aria-label` when there is no visible label), as the input is. - **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears. - The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps the option's full contrast on the highlighted row. - The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear selection". - `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, and the helper text is the input's description. - Loading and empty states are announced from the list. - After an option is picked with the pointer, the input loses focus and the field returns to rest (no caret, no ring). A keyboard pick keeps focus in the input, so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page. - Options are 32px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to 44px, and the clear and open buttons get a 44×44px hit area.
