import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories' # Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick a value for a form, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs). ## Variants Menu has one look. What changes is the kind of entry in `items`, and a menu can mix them: | Entry | Use for | | --- | --- | | Action (the default) | Something to do now: Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Closes the menu. `isDestructive` draws it in the danger colour. | | Link (`href`) | Going somewhere: Documentation, Settings. A real ``. | | Submenu (`items`) | A set of choices that belongs under one item: Move to, Share with. | | Checkbox (`type: 'checkbox'`) | Settings that are on or off, several at a time: Show hidden files. Keeps the menu open. | | Radio (`type: 'radio'`) | One of a few settings: Sort by name, date or size. Keeps the menu open. | | Group (`type: 'group'`) and separator | Structure for a longer menu: a label over related items, a rule between sets. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menu.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu) - Behaviour: [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A link item has the same parts as an action. Checkbox and radio items show a check where an action shows its icon, so their labels line up. ## Measurements The popup is the Select list's surface. Each item is a row of the md control tier, with the normal pad: its text is left-aligned. The item's corner nests inside the popup's: the popup radius minus the popup padding, so the highlight runs parallel to the popup edge. The popup is at least 12rem wide, or the trigger's width if that is wider, and no taller than the space on screen: past that it scrolls. It opens 4px from the trigger. ## Color The destructive item uses the danger text colour, not the solid: it reads at 4.5:1 on the popup and on its highlight. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: a `--accent` fill, the icon taking the text colour. A submenu's item stays highlighted while its submenu is open. Focus moves with the highlight, so there is no separate focus ring inside the popup. - **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity and skipped by the arrow keys (Archive, above). - **Checked** checkbox and radio items show the check; unchecked ones keep the empty column. - The trigger's own hover, focus and pressed states are the [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)'s. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`items` is data, like Select's `options`, not child components. `shortcut` is display only: binding the key is left to the page, which knows what else is bound. ## When to use Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give destructive actions the last place, after a separator. } doCaption="Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour." dont={} dontCaption="Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen." /> } doCaption="A menu of actions. Each item does something now." dont={} dontCaption="A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name." /> ## When not to use - **To pick a value for a form.** Use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list is long enough to search. - **For one or two actions.** Show them as [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action is one fewer person finds. - **For the app's main navigation.** Use a [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where the reader is. - **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds only menu items. ## Accessibility - The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and `aria-disabled` on disabled items. - Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. - Toggles keep the menu open, so several can be changed in one go; actions close it and focus returns to the trigger. - The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the item. Give `textValue` when a label is not plain text, or typeahead cannot find it. - A disabled link has no `href`, so it cannot be followed. - Items are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while the menu is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as MenubarStories from './Menubar.stories' # Menubar A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, each opening a flyout of commands. Use it in an editor-like screen with more commands than a toolbar can show. ## Variants Menubar has one look. Each flyout is a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) popup and takes the same entries: actions with shortcuts, links, submenus, checkbox and radio items, groups and separators. | Menu | Use for | | --- | --- | | Enabled (the default) | Commands that apply now. | | Disabled (`disabled`) | A menu that does not apply in the current state. It stays in place, muted, so the bar does not shift. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Menubar } from 'zweihander/menubar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menubar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu) - Behaviour: [Base UI Menubar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The flyout on this tab is a picture: it is drawn open in place, not positioned over the page. Its parts are Menu's; see [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for the item's own anatomy. ## Measurements The bar is a strip: its triggers are rows of the sm control tier, one step shorter than the md items in the flyout. Triggers sit inset from the bar edge by the same amount as items inside a Menu popup, and their corner nests inside the bar's the same way. A flyout opens 4px below its trigger, lined up with the trigger's start edge. When the bar is wider than its container, it scrolls sideways. ## Color The flyout's colours are Menu's. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, { label: 'Disabled menu', content: }, ]} /> - **Hover and highlighted**: the trigger takes the same `--accent` fill as a highlighted item in the flyout. - **Open**: the trigger keeps that fill while its flyout is open, so the reader sees which menu they are in. - **Focus**: a keyboard focus ring inside the trigger, so it does not collide with its neighbours. - **Disabled**: muted at 60% opacity, no fill on hover, skipped by the arrow keys. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`menus` is data, and each menu's `items` is Menu's `items`. Shortcuts are plain trailing text, as in Menu: display only, binding the key is left to the page. ### Differences from the spec - **No navigation menu.** The source pairs a menubar with a navigation menu: links in flyouts, each with a description. Zweihänder leaves that out: app navigation is the Nav Sidebar and the Top Bar's links, which show the current page; a flyout of described links is a marketing-site pattern. - **No item description.** Flyout items are Menu's entries, one line each. A second line of text is what a navigation menu needs, and it is not built. ## When to use Use a Menubar in a screen that works like a desktop tool, an invoice or report editor, a spreadsheet, where people look for commands by category and learn their shortcuts. Name each menu for what it holds and keep the order people know from desktop apps: File, Edit, View, then your own, then Help. } doCaption="Commands, grouped by the familiar File, Edit, View, with their shortcuts." dont={} dontCaption="Pages behind flyouts. Navigation belongs in the Nav Sidebar or the Top Bar, where the current page shows." /> ## When not to use - **For the app's navigation.** Use a [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or the [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs)'s links: they show where the reader is, a menubar does not. - **For a few actions on one thing.** Use a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a button, or Buttons. - **To find any command by name.** Add a [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-command-palette--docs); it can sit alongside the menubar. ## Accessibility - The bar is a `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label`. Each trigger is a `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; a disabled menu's trigger has `aria-disabled`. - The bar is one tab stop. Arrow Left and Right move along the triggers, skipping disabled menus. - Arrow Down, Enter or Space on a trigger opens its flyout on the first item. Inside a flyout the keys are Menu's. - With a flyout open, Arrow Right and Left move to the next and previous menu and open it, and moving the pointer onto another trigger opens that menu instead. - Escape closes the flyout and returns focus to its trigger; choosing an action closes it too. - Shortcuts and icons are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the item. - Triggers are 24px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) their hit area grows to 44px. - `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while a flyout is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories' # Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page numbers around the current one. Under a table it can also say which rows are shown ("21–40 of 340") and let the reader pick how many rows a page holds. ## Variants Pagination has one look. What changes is the size, how many numbers show, whether the pages are buttons or links, and the two optional ends. | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Under a table or a list of results. The default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a card, a side panel, a compact table footer. | | `getHref` | Pages with their own URL: each page is a link that can be opened in a new tab and shared. | | Buttons | Pages that only exist in this view's state, such as a filtered list in a dialog. The default. | | `totalItems` | A table footer, where the reader needs to know how many rows there are: adds the summary at the start. | | `pageSizeOptions` | Long tables where readers scan in bulk: adds a "Rows per page" select at the end. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/pagination.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination) - Behaviour: a plain `
` around a list of buttons or links - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The first and last page always show, the current page keeps a sibling each side, and "…" appears only where it hides two or more pages. A single hidden page is shown instead, since "…" would take the same room. So the number of controls stays the same as you move through the middle, and Next does not jump. The summary and the select only appear when `totalItems` and `pageSizeOptions` are passed. The summary sits at the start and pushes the pages and the select to the end; on a narrow screen the row wraps. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A control is square at its minimum; the inline padding only shows on a page number of three digits or more. Previous and next have no padding, so they stay square. ## Color One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. At rest a control has no fill. ## States - **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--primary`, medium weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing. - **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--accent` chip. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the control. - **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50% opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their `href`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
The rows-per-page select is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) at the same `size`. Changing it moves to the page that holds the first row shown before, so the reader does not lose their place; it calls `onPageSizeChange`, then `onPageChange` if the page moved. Every other `
` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page, total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own. ## When to use Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's position stable as pages change. Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer. } doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line." dont={} dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page." /> Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is. Offer `pageSizeOptions` only when readers really scan in bulk; three or four choices (10, 20, 50, 100) are enough. When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new tab, bookmarked and shared. ## When not to use - **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): page numbers mean nothing in a stream. - **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all. - **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper. - **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Pagination", around a list. - Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page". - At either end, Previous or Next is disabled. As links they lose their `href` (the only thing that stops an `` navigating) and keep `role="link"` with `aria-disabled`, so they are still announced as a disabled link. - With `getHref`, each control is a real ``; without it, a native `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories' # Stepper Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up, checkout, a setup wizard. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Horizontal (default) | Three to five steps above a form. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. | | Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. | | `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. | | Bullets (`appearance="bullets"`) | A phone, a narrow dialog, or more steps than fit with labels: only the current step's label shows, "Step 3 of 4: Invite", over a row of dots. | | Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper) - Behaviour: a plain `
` around an ordered list - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The last step has no connector. Vertical, the connector runs down from each marker, beside the text. ## Measurements The marker's ring and the connector are 2px. The current dot's ring is 2px wide, 2px clear of the dot, in the dot's own colour. Horizontal, a connector runs along the markers' centre line from one marker to the next, `--space-2` clear of each. ## Color Complete and current share the primary colour: the filled disc says done, the ring says here. The current ring uses `--primary-text`, the step of the accent that reads at 4.5:1 on the page, because it frames a number. ## States A step's status is its state. With `onStepClick`, finished steps and the current one are buttons, with hover and focus of their own. }, { label: 'Clickable' }, { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' }, ]} > - **Hover** underlines the label of a clickable step. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the step. - **Upcoming** steps are never buttons, so they have no hover or focus. - With bullets, **hover** fills the dot's hit area with `--muted`, since there is no visible label to underline. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through. A step's `status` is only for the exception, such as an error: the rest is worked out from `current`. Only finished steps can be clicked; upcoming ones stay text, because a flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs. Bullets ignore `orientation` and draw no connectors: the dots sit close enough to read as one line. When `current` is past the last step, the "Step 3 of 4" line is left out. A step with an error that is also `current` keeps `aria-current` and the ring. ## When to use Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each. } doCaption="Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper." /> ## When not to use - **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs). - **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs). - **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page promises steps that are not there. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of steps and the position of each. - The current step has `aria-current="step"`. - The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in visually hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started", "Workspace, has an error". Bullets hide every label but the current one, and still say each in the same hidden text. Their visible "Step 3 of 4: Invite" is hidden from screen readers, which hear the list instead. - An error on the current step keeps `aria-current="step"`. - Without `onStepClick` nothing is focusable. With it, complete and current steps are real buttons: reached with Tab, pressed with Enter or Space, showing the focus ring, and 44px tall on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories' # Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activity, Settings of one project. ## Variants `appearance` is the look. Either takes either size and orientation. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `underline` | The sections of a page or a panel. Tabs sit on a 1px rule; a bar slides under the selected one. The default. | | `pills` | A compact view switch in a toolbar, such as List / Board. A segmented track with the selected tab lifted. | | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `isFullWidth` | Two to four tabs that should fill a narrow container, such as a side panel or a phone screen. | | `vertical` | Many sections, or labels too long for a row: settings pages, a panel beside its content. | | Icons | Recognisable icons beside the label. Never an icon alone: the label is the tab's name. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tabs } from 'zweihander/tabs' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tabs.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The indicator is one element for the whole list. It moves to the selected tab rather than each tab drawing its own, so a change of tab slides it across. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A tab is a button in a row, so it takes the spacious inline padding. The underline indicator is 2px. In `pills`, the track has a 2px inset and the chip's corner is the track's minus 2px, so the two stay concentric at every size. ## Color Each appearance has its own label colours and indicator. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. Pill labels use `--subtle-foreground`, not `--muted-foreground`: that is 4.3:1 on the `--muted` track, under 4.5:1. ## States - **Selected**: the label takes the selected colour and the indicator slides under it (`underline`) or behind it (`pills`). - **Hover** brings an unselected label up to `--foreground`. It adds no fill. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn just inside the tab, so it is not clipped by the list. - **Disabled** (Archive, above) is the enabled look at 50% opacity. It still takes focus. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely, in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time. Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long ones push the row past its container. } doCaption="Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical." /> Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does. Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on `activateOnFocus` only for light panels. ## When not to use - **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a Stepper. - **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put things that are read together on the same view. - **To go to another page.** Use links, a Nav Sidebar or Breadcrumbs: a tab changes the view, not the URL. - **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group: that changes a value, not the view. ## Accessibility - `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab. - One tab stop: Tab moves into the list on the selected tab and the next Tab moves on to the panel. - Arrow keys move between tabs (Left and Right, or Up and Down when vertical, with `aria-orientation` set); Home and End jump to the ends. - Arrows move focus without selecting; Enter or Space selects. With `activateOnFocus`, arrows select as they go. - A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is found and announced, but it cannot be selected. - Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, drawn inside the tab.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories' # Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked. ## Variants `variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. | | `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. | | `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. | | `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. | | `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. | | `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert) - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content without a jump in size. The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so switching appearance never moves the content. ## Color Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in `--foreground`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so the colour goes on the icon and the title. ## States The alert itself has no states. Its close button does. - **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, inside the button's edge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the top by the page. - **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in your state and can be remembered across visits. ## When to use Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it means and what to do. } doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step." dont={} dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do." /> The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too: "Upload failed", not just a red box. ## When not to use - **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes away by itself. - **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs). - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal. ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt. - An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen reader to finish. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The close button is a native `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories' # Inline Alert A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no title and no close button: "Changes are saved automatically", "Couldn't reach the server". ## Variants `variant` is the colour, by meaning, and the whole line takes it. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `info` | A fact about what is above it: "Changes are saved automatically." | | `success` | A check that passed: "Domain verified." | | `warning` | A consequence to know before going on: "This link expires in 24 hours." | | `danger` | Something that failed: "Couldn't reach the server." | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { InlineAlert } from 'zweihander/inline-alert' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-alert.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx) - Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The icon box is one line tall, so on a message that wraps it stays on the first line. ## Measurements No padding, border or background: it lines up with the text and fields around it. ## Color The whole line, icon and message, takes the variant's text colour. An Alert can keep its message in `--foreground` because its box carries the colour; an inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is 4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays readable. The action keeps its own colours: a Link or a Button, as passed. ## States The message has no states. An action in it has its own. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Inline Alert for a short message about the thing right above it: a group of fields, a whole form, a section. A failed submit is the common case. } doCaption="An error about one field goes on the field, as its helper text: it is read when the field is focused." dont={} dontCaption="An inline alert under a field is not tied to it: a screen reader in the field never hears it." /> ## When not to use - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a message about a whole page or region**, or one that needs a title, an action row or a close button. Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs). - **For news about something that just happened.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs). ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default, read in order with the page. - `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The action is whatever you pass (a Link, a Button) and keeps its own keyboard behaviour and focus ring.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ToastStories from './Toast.stories' # Toast A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just happened: saved, sent, moved, failed. It closes itself after a few seconds and never blocks the page. Try it: the toast opens in the corner of this window. ## Variants `variant` colours the icon only; the message stays in the surface's text colour. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `default` | Most toasts: something done, nothing to judge. "File moved to Trash." | | `info` | A neutral fact about what just happened: "Sync paused while offline." | | `success` | A result worth confirming because it was not obvious: "Invite sent to 12 people." | | `warning` | Done, with a catch: "Saved, but 2 rows were skipped." | | `danger` | Something failed. Interrupts the screen reader. Say what to do next, and keep the way to do it on the page too. | `promise()` adds a loading toast that becomes `success` or `danger` when the promise settles. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'zweihander/toast' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toast.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toast](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toast) - Behaviour: [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the title, or the description alone, is required. The icon box is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. Toasts stack with a gap, the newest nearest the edge they grow from. At most 24rem wide, and never wider than the window less the edge distance on both sides. ## Color The surface takes the opposite appearance to the page: dark toasts on a light page, light on a dark one. The contrast pulls the eye to a message that is only there for a few seconds. The tokens below are read in that opposite appearance. `default` shows no icon. ## States }, ]} > - **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`. Hovering the stack also pauses every toast's timer. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline inside the action or the close button. Focus in the stack pauses the timers too. - **Pending** is a `promise()` toast: a spinner in place of the icon, and no timer until it settles. - **Entering** fades in and slides `--space-2` from the edge the stack grows from; **leaving** fades out. With reduced motion, only the fade. ## API `ToastProvider` wraps the app once: {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`useToast()`, anywhere inside it, shows and closes toasts: ```tsx const toast = useToast() toast.add({ title: 'File moved to Trash', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } }) ``` {/* Markdown tables do not scroll by themselves on a phone either. */}
| `useToast()` | | | --- | --- | | `add(options)` | Shows a toast, returns its id. | | `update(id, options)` | Changes one in place; only the options given change. | | `close(id?)` | Closes one, or all. | | `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | A loading toast that becomes success or danger when the promise settles. | | Option | Values | | | --- | --- | --- | | `title`, `description` | node | | | `variant` | `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `default` | | `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | One button. | | `timeout` | number (ms) | The provider's by default. `0` keeps it until dismissed. | | `priority` | `low`, `high` | `high` by default for `danger`. | | `onClose` | function | |
### Differences from the spec - **Bottom right by default**, where the spec suggests top right. `placement` takes any corner or edge centre. ## When to use Use a Toast to confirm something the reader just did, when the result is not already visible: moved, sent, copied, saved in the background. Offer "Undo" when it can be undone. } doCaption="News about something just done, with a way to undo it. Undo is also reachable from the Trash." dont={} dontCaption="A problem the reader has to fix goes away in a few seconds. Put it in an Alert on the page." /> Keep it to a few words. A toast is read in passing, often half-noticed. ## When not to use - **For something the reader must act on, or might need to read twice.** Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs) on the page, or a Modal for a decision. - **For an error in a form.** Use the field's own error, or an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) under the form. - **As the only way to an action.** The toast goes away; the same action ("Undo") must be reachable somewhere else. - **To confirm what is already visible.** A row that appears in a table needs no "Row added" toast. ## Accessibility - The stack is a polite live region: a new toast is announced without interrupting. `danger` toasts (and any with `priority: 'high'`) are `role="alertdialog"` and announced at once. - Each toast is a non-modal dialog named by its title, or by its description when it has none (as `promise()` toasts do). - Timers pause while the pointer is over the stack or focus is in it, so there is time to reach the action. F6 moves focus to the stack. - The close button is named `Dismiss`; Enter and Space press it. On touch screens its hit area grows to 44×44px, and a toast swipes away toward the nearest edge. - A toast raised from inside a modal shows above it and is not hidden from assistive tech by it.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ConfirmDialogStories from './ConfirmDialog.stories' # Confirm Dialog Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a question, what it will destroy, then Cancel or the action. A press outside does nothing, so the reader has to choose. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Default | An everyday delete: a comment, a file, a saved view. One question, two buttons. | | Type to confirm (`confirmText`) | A large delete that cannot be undone: a workspace, an account, a project with its files. The action waits until the reader types the name. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ConfirmDialog } from 'zweihander/confirm-dialog' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/confirm-dialog.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) (the alert dialog) - Built on: [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, on [Base UI Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open dialogs on this tab and the next are pictures: rendered in a frame with `container` and `isModal={false}`, inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements It is a Modal at `size="sm"` (at most 24rem wide): container, title, description, body and footer take Modal's measurements. Its own parts: The icon is one line of the title tall, so it stays on the first line when the title wraps. ## Color Everything else takes Modal's colours, and the buttons keep their own: Cancel is `secondary` outlined, the action `destructive`. ## States The dialog is open or closed. With `confirmText`, the action is disabled until the field matches, then enabled; without it, it is enabled from the start. }, { label: 'Ready', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Differences from the spec - **Destructive only.** There is no neutral variant: a decision that destroys nothing (sign out, leave without saving) is a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, where you choose the buttons. - **No pending state.** The dialog closes on confirm. If the delete can fail, control `open` and keep it open until your request settles. ## When to use Before an action that destroys something the reader cannot get back. Put the object's name in the title, say in the description what goes with it, and name the action button after what it does. Type to confirm is for the few deletes that are both large and final. Used on every delete, it becomes a chore readers do without reading. } doCaption="Ask once for an everyday delete, with the action on the button." dont={} dontCaption="Do not make the reader type for a small delete: it teaches them to type without reading." /> ## When not to use - **When the action can be undone.** Do it, then offer Undo in a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): no question is faster than a good one. - **For a decision that destroys nothing**, such as Sign out or Leave without saving. Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`. - **To show a warning.** Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="alertdialog"`, named by the title (the icon is hidden from assistive tech) and described by the consequence. - Focus starts on Cancel, so Enter on open cannot delete. With `confirmText` it starts in the field, which is named "To confirm, type" and the name. - The action stays disabled until the field matches exactly, case included; spaces around the text are ignored. Enter in the field confirms once it matches. - A press outside does nothing. Cancel and Escape close it without confirming, and focus goes back to the trigger. - Reopened, the field starts empty.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as DrawerStories from './Drawer.stories' # Drawer A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen, over the page, for work that sits beside what the reader was doing: filters, a quick look at a record, a short form. ## Variants | Side | Use for | | --- | --- | | Right (default) | Details and editing: a quick look at a record from its list, a create or edit form, notifications. | | Left | Content tied to the left of the page, such as a panel for the list or tree beside it. | | Bottom | A short sheet as tall as its content: share, a few actions, a picker. Works best on a phone. | `size` sets the width of a side drawer: `sm` (20rem) for filters, `md` (28rem) for a form, `lg` (40rem) for a record with a lot to show. A side drawer always leaves a touch target's width of backdrop, so on a phone it is nearly full width and can still be tapped away. For short content on a phone, pick `bottom` yourself: the side does not change with the screen. Taller than the screen, the body scrolls and the header and footer stay in view. On a touch screen it can also be swiped back towards its edge. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Drawer, DrawerClose } from 'zweihander/drawer' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/drawer.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Drawer.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Drawer.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/drawer](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/drawer) - Behaviour: [Base UI Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open drawers on this tab and the next are pictures: real drawers rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements A side drawer is full height and at most 20rem (`sm`), 28rem (`md`) or 40rem (`lg`) wide. A bottom sheet is full width and as tall as its content, up to the screen less `--target-coarse`. Borders are 1px: on the edge that faces the page, under the header and over the footer. Backdrop and drawer sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and slide in over `--duration-base`. ## Color Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button. ## States The drawer is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and slides the container in from its edge; closing reverses it. During a swipe the container follows the finger and the backdrop fades with it. The close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the button with `--accent`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`DrawerClose` closes the drawer it is in. Give it your own button with `render`: `}>Cancel`. ### Differences from the spec - **No push mode.** A drawer always covers the page with a scrim. A panel that pushes the page aside is part of the page's layout, not an overlay: build it into the page. - **No top side.** Nothing in a business app slides down from the top that a Menu or a Toast does not already cover. ## When to use Use a drawer when the reader needs the context behind it: a record looked at from its list, filters for the table they are reading, a form that fills in something on the page. The page stays visible, dimmed, at its place. } doCaption="Show a record from its list in a drawer: the list stays in place behind it, where the reader left it." dont={} dontCaption="Do not ask a yes-or-no question at the edge of the screen. A decision belongs in a Modal with isAlert." /> Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Clear) in the `secondary` variant. A form that would lose its input sets `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. ## When not to use - **For a decision or a confirmation.** Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, or a [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) before a delete: it sits in the middle, where the reader is looking. - **For a small form tied to one button.** Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside the button and leaves the page usable. - **For site navigation.** Keep it in the sidebar; on a phone the sidebar folds to its icon rail. - **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own. - **Over another drawer or a modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it. ## Accessibility - `role="dialog"`, named by the title and described by the description. - Opening moves focus to the drawer itself, so its title and description are read first and a phone does not pop up its keyboard; Tab then reaches the close button. Focus is trapped inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden` and its scroll is locked. Closing returns focus to the trigger. - The body is a tab stop after the close button, so a keyboard can scroll a long body of text. - `initialFocus` sends focus to another element on open, such as the first field of a form. - Escape, a press outside the drawer and the close button each close it. The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`). Swiping is never the only way out. - With `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`, a press outside does nothing; Escape still closes it. - A Select opened inside a drawer lists its options above it: both sit at `--layer-overlay`, and the one opened last is on top. - `side` is physical: on a right-to-left page a right drawer is still on the right, and swipes right to close.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories' # Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed and out of reach until it closes. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Dialog (default) | A short task on its own: edit a profile, invite people. A close button, Escape and a press on the backdrop all close it. | | Alert (`isAlert`) | A decision with consequences: delete, discard, leave. No close button and a press on the backdrop does nothing, so it ends only through its own buttons or Escape. | `size` sets the maximum width: `sm` (24rem) for an alert, `md` (32rem) for a short form, `lg` (48rem) for long content. Taller than the screen, the body scrolls and the title and footer stay in view. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Modal, ModalClose } from 'zweihander/modal' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/modal.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) - Behaviour: [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open modals on this tab and the next are pictures: real modals rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements Width is `size`: at most 24rem (`sm`), 32rem (`md`) or 48rem (`lg`), and never wider than the screen less its margin. The border is 1px. Backdrop and modal sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-base`. ## Color Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button. ## States The modal is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and scales the container up from 97%; closing reverses it. The close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the button with `--accent`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button, so it is not clipped at the container's corner. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with `render`: `}>Cancel`. ## When to use Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. Use one when the task must be finished or abandoned before going on, or for a decision with consequences. For a decision, use `isAlert`, say exactly what will happen in the description, and name the buttons after what they do. Before a delete or anything else that cannot be undone, use a [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs): it is this alert with the warning, the focus on Cancel and type to confirm built in. } doCaption="Name the buttons after what they do: Delete, Keep project. The choice reads without the question." dont={} dontCaption="OK and Cancel make the reader go back to the question to know which one deletes." /> Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Keep) in the `secondary` variant. ## When not to use - **For a small form tied to one button**, such as Share or a filter. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside the button and leaves the page usable. - **For information**: a success, a warning, a tip. Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) or a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs); neither stops the reader. - **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own. - **Over another modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it. ## Accessibility - `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described by the description. - Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`, and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing returns focus to the trigger. - `isModal={false}` drops the focus trap, the scroll lock and the hidden page, but the backdrop still covers the page. It is for pictures of a modal, such as the ones on these tabs: a real modal stays modal. - Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its own buttons (and Escape). - **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all sit at `--layer-overlay`. Each portals to the end of `` when it opens, so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal lists its options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would hide. - The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`), has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories' # Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you close it. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. | | Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. | | `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover, when what it holds must be reachable by click, keyboard and touch. For a person or record preview on a link, use [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). | A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/popover.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the trigger where it opens. ## Measurements The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px border and a semibold title. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon, one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-fast`. ## Color Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--popover`, its border and shadow. ## States The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it: share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links, inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not. } doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action." dont={} dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal." /> ## When not to use - **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). - **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs. - **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs). ## Accessibility - The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`. - Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger. - **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped, page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked. - Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus, then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible. - `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content stays reachable by keyboard and touch. - The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories' import { HoverCard } from './Tooltip' # Tooltip A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint. Its sibling `HoverCard` previews a person or record behind a link. ## Variants | Variant | When to use | |---|---| | Tooltip | A label or a one-line hint on a control. | | Hover card | A preview of a person or record on a link to it: avatar, name, meta and an optional action. | The tooltip opens on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus at once. Wrap a row of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` so that once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay: Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover or focus the triggers above to see them. ### Hover card `HoverCard` opens after 600ms of hover or focus on a link and stays open for 300ms after the pointer leaves, so the pointer can cross to it. It is drawn like a Popover, a raised surface, not an inverted label: Hover the name to open the real one: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { HoverCard, Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from 'zweihander/tooltip' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tooltip.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip), [Base UI Preview Card](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open tooltips on this tab and the next are pictures: real tooltips held open and rendered in place with `container`, laid out above the trigger where they open. The hover card, open under its link: ## Measurements The container is as wide as its text, at most 20rem and never wider than the room beside the trigger; longer text wraps. It opens 6px from the trigger, on the `--layer-tooltip` layer, above popovers and modals, so a tooltip on a control inside one still shows. It fades in over `--duration-fast`. The hover card is as wide as its content, at most 20rem. It opens 6px under the link, start-aligned, on the `--layer-overlay` layer with Popover, below tooltips. ## Color The tooltip is inverted in both modes: a tooltip is not part of the page, and the dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same contrast as body text. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Closed** until the pointer rests on the trigger for `delay` (300ms), or the trigger takes keyboard focus, which opens it at once. - **Open** until Escape, blur or the pointer leaves, after `closeDelay`. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 96%. - The trigger keeps the states of its own component; the tooltip has none of its own. - The hover card has the same two states, after `delay` (600ms) of hover or focus and `closeDelay` (300ms) after the pointer leaves both the link and the card. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TooltipGroup` is Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`: tooltips inside it share one delay. ### HoverCard
## When to use Use a Tooltip for a label or a hint: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, one line on what a control does. 300ms before it opens is quick enough to feel responsive and long enough that tooltips do not flash as the pointer crosses a toolbar. } doCaption="A short label that repeats the icon-only button's name for sighted users." dont={} dontCaption="Rules the reader needs to fill the field. Touch cannot open a tooltip, and it hides as soon as focus moves on: put the rules under the field." /> ## When not to use - **For anything a reader needs to finish a task.** Put it on the page: a tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it disappears the moment you look away. - **For links, buttons or other interactive content.** Hover and touch cannot reach the tooltip. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). - **For a rich preview.** A tooltip holds text only. To preview a person or record behind a link, use `HoverCard`. Its action is a shortcut, so the linked page must offer the same action. - **On a disabled button.** It is not focusable, so its tooltip never opens by keyboard. Put the reason it is disabled in text next to it. ## Accessibility - It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave. - Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description. - It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs its own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted users too. - The trigger must be focusable: a Button, a link, a field. - `--background` on `--foreground` reads at 16:1 or more in both modes. ### Hover card - The trigger is a link to what the card previews. Hover or keyboard focus on it opens the card; Escape closes it. - The card is a visual preview, not a dialog: focus stays on the link and Tab moves past the card, its action included. Touch has no hover, so everything on it must be on the page the link opens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories' # Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it is empty, and what to do about it. ## Variants There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The component is the same; the words and the action are not. | Kind | Use for | | --- | --- | | First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. | | No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. | | Cleared out | Everything is done. patterns-application-ui-action-panel--do.title: Patterns/Application UI/Action Panel
patterns-application-ui-action-panel--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ActionPanelStories from './ActionPanel.stories'

<Meta of={ActionPanelStories} />

# Action Panel

A [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) that offers one action:
a title saying what it does, a description of what happens when you take
it, and the control that does it. For actions that stand on their own on a
settings or detail page, such as exporting data, renewing a plan or
deleting a workspace. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Forms: Action
panels.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/action-panel.json
```

## Simple

A button under the description. The default, and the right one when the
description runs to two lines or more.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Simple} />

## Button at the end

`actionPlacement="end"` puts the action beside the text, for a short
description. It drops under the text when the card gets narrow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.ButtonAtEnd} />

## With a switch

A setting that takes effect the moment it changes, so there is no Save
button. Give the Switch an `aria-label` that matches the title: the
panel's title is not its label.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithSwitch} />

## With an input

A small form, one field and its button, for an action that needs one
value. The form is yours: the panel lays out what you pass.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithInput} />

## Danger

`variant="danger"` edges the panel in the destructive colour, in every
appearance, flat surface included. Use it only for what cannot be undone,
with a destructive Button, and confirm in a
[Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) before acting. Put it
last on the page.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Danger} />

## Without a description

The description is optional; several actions wrap onto more rows rather
than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.TitleOnly} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ActionPanelStories} />

Every other Card prop and `<div>` attribute passes through, except
`onClick`, `render` and `orientation`: the panel is not itself a control,
and its placement prop sets the direction.

## Layout

- **Below** stacks the text and the action, in the Card's gap.
- **End** keeps the text at least 16rem wide, then wraps the action under
  it, keeping its order.
- The description stops at 65 characters a line; long titles and words
  break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

- **With link**: no slot of its own. Pass a [Link](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs)
  as the `action`.
- **Simple well, with well**: not a variant. The tinted inset is the
  Card's look; pick it with `appearance` so the panel matches the other
  blocks on the page.
- **Danger** is added: Tailwind leaves a danger zone to a red button.

## Accessibility

- The panel is a `group` named by its title, so a screen reader names
  it when focus enters the control. The description is linked with
  `aria-describedby`; screen readers differ on reading a group's
  description, so the control's own name must make sense alone. The title
  is heard twice in reading order, as the heading and the group's name.
- The title is an `h2` by default. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The danger edge is not the only warning: the title and the destructive
  button say it too, so it does not rest on colour.
- The control keeps its own name: a Switch needs an `aria-label`, a
  button names its action ("Delete workspace", not "Delete"), a field
  has its label.

patterns-application-ui-app-content--doc.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AppContentStories from './AppContent.stories'

<Meta of={AppContentStories} />

# App Content

The page region of an app: the `main` landmark. One of the three pieces
the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places;
the shell puts it around its children, so you rarely render it yourself.
It reads the shell's grid and canvas, so it is not used on its own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-content.json
```

## Flat

The Theme's `contentStyle="flat"` (the default): one card surface, inset
8px from the shell's edges at every density. Blocks inside are
[Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) with
`appearance="surface"`, which become sections ruled off at the top.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.Flat} />

## On the canvas

`contentStyle="card"`: no surface; the page sits on the canvas and each
surface Card is raised.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.OnCanvas} />

## Props

Any `main` attribute; the App Shell passes the `id` its skip link targets.
`aside` takes a column for beside the page, in an `aside` landmark named by
`asideLabel`; the App Shell passes both through
([With an aside](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs)).

## Layout

- Below 48rem the flat surface drops its inset, edge and rounding and goes
  flush.
- The page padding is `--space-container`, `--space-section` from 64rem.
  App Content sets no maximum width: to cap and centre a page, put a
  [Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-container--docs) inside it.
- Only the page scrolls; the shell's other pieces stay put. With an aside,
  from 80rem the page and the aside scroll on their own, side by side;
  under 80rem the aside follows the page and they scroll as one.
- The surface restates `--background` as `--card` (flat) or as the
  canvas's solid colour (card), so components that draw "the surface under
  me" match it.

## Accessibility

- The `main` landmark, focusable (`tabIndex={-1}`) so the shell's skip
  link can move focus to it.
- An aside is a `complementary` landmark after `main`, focusable so a
  keyboard can scroll it.
- On a canvas, text takes the canvas text colours (the Theme's
  `canvas-foreground` and `canvas-muted-foreground` tokens); the kit checks
  them for its own canvases.

import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CardHeadingStories from './CardHeading.stories'

<Meta of={CardHeadingStories} />

# Card Heading

The top row of a card: what the card is, a line of context, and what you
can do with it. Put it first inside a [Card](?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs);
the card's padding and gap space it from the content. After Tailwind UI
Application UI, Headings: Card headings.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card-heading.json
```

## Simple

A title and, optionally, one line of description.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With action

The card's main action at the end of the title row. One primary button at
most; a card is part of a page that has its own primary action.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAction} />

## With avatar and menu

Who or what the card is about, as an Avatar or an Icon before the title.
Rarely used actions go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays
short.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAvatarAndMenu} />

## With a rule

The heading draws no line of its own. When the content needs setting off,
put a [Divider](?path=/docs/atomic-elements-divider--docs) after the heading,
inside the card.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithIconAndRule} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={CardHeadingStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title and description
  keep the row down to 16rem, then the actions drop underneath them,
  keeping their order.
- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The title is an `h2` by default: a card on a page sits under the
  page's `h1`. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` when the card sits under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The media is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title
  already says who or what the card is about.
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button. When a card
  repeats on a page, make action names unique, e.g. "Edit Chelsea Hagon".
