import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CommonActionsStories from './CommonActions.stories'

<Meta of={CommonActionsStories} />

# Common Actions

The actions every record and form shares (Create, Edit, Save, Cancel,
Delete and the rest), each with one label, one place, one button style,
one level of confirmation and, where the platform already has one, one
shortcut. After Carbon's Common actions pattern, cut to what an enterprise
app repeats on every object.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/common-actions.json
```

It installs `commonActions`, the table below as data, and
`CommonActionsTable`, which renders it. Place a button by reading its row:

```tsx
import { commonActions } from './CommonActions'

<Button type="submit" {...commonActions.save.button}>{commonActions.save.label}</Button>
```

There is no `<SaveButton>`: the buttons stay Button, Menu entries and
Confirm Dialogs, and the catalogue only decides which. Rename a label or
change a level in your copy, and the table follows. A pattern usually owns
no data; this one is conventions, not records, so it ships them as data
the table and your code can both read.

## Reference

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.Reference} />

## Placement

**Form footer.** Cancel, then Save, at the end. Save is the submit button
and the only primary one in the form. [Form
Layouts](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)'
`FormActions` lays them out.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.FormFooter} />

**List header.** Import and Export, then Create as the page's one primary
button, at the end of the [Card
Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs) or page
header.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.ListHeader} />

**Record header.** Edit next to the title; everything else in the overflow
menu, Delete last after a separator so it is never the item under the
pointer when the menu opens. A list row puts the same entries in its ⋯
menu ([Stacked List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs),
[Grid List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-grid-list--docs)).

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.RecordHeader} />

## Confirmation

Ask in proportion to what is lost. Each step up costs every user a click
on every use, so the level follows how hard the action is to reverse, not
how serious it sounds.

| Level | When | Built with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Easy to reverse, or nothing is lost: Edit, Duplicate, Export | The button |
| Undo toast | Reversible, but the result leaves the screen: Archive, Remove | [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs) with an Undo action |
| Confirm Dialog | Cannot be undone: Delete | [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) |
| Type to confirm | Cannot be undone and takes other records with it: a workspace, a ledger | Confirm Dialog with `confirmText`, from a danger [Action Panel](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-action-panel--docs) |

Delete is a Confirm Dialog by default and goes up to type to confirm when
it cascades, so no row of the table names that level. An Undo toast times
out: keep the action reachable elsewhere too (an Archived filter, the
record's menu) for anyone who misses it. The dialog's own Cancel is
outlined, beside its contained destructive button; that is Confirm
Dialog's, not a second Cancel style.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.ArchiveWithUndo} />
<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.DeleteWithConfirm} />
<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.TypeToConfirm} />

## Labels

- **One verb, sentence case.** Add the object only when the page has more
  than one kind: "Create invoice" in a header, "Delete" in an invoice's own
  menu.
- **The pairs are not synonyms.** Create makes a record, Add puts one into
  a set; Delete destroys it, Remove takes it out of the set; Cancel throws
  input away, Close has none to throw.
- **The confirm button repeats the action** ("Delete invoice"), never
  "OK" or "Yes".

## Shortcuts

Only shortcuts the platform already teaches: ⌘S, Esc, ⌘Z. Shown as
[Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) in Mac glyphs; show Ctrl for
⌘ on other systems. The app binds them; the catalogue only names them. A
shortcut for anything else belongs in the [Command
Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-command-palette--docs), where it can be
found.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={CommonActionsStories} />

`commonActions` is keyed by id (`save`, `delete`, …); each entry has
`label`, `purpose`, `placement`, `confirm` (`none`, `undo`, `dialog` or
`typed`), and optionally `button` (`variant` and `appearance`; left out
for an action that only lives in a menu) and `shortcut`.

## Layout

- **No breakpoint of its own.** The form footer and the headers wrap their
  buttons when the row runs out of room; Save stays last.
- **The reference table** scrolls sideways in a narrow container, as any
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Carbon's Common actions, and where this departs from them:

- **Fewer actions.** Clear, Reset, Copy, Refresh, Search and a wizard's
  Back and Next are left out: they belong to Filter Bar, Search, Steps
  and their own components, which already place them.
- **Archive and Undo are added**, because an ERP keeps records with
  transactions and reverses rather than asks.
- **The trigger for Delete is outlined**, as on Action Panel; only the
  dialog's confirm button is filled.

## Accessibility

- Cancel comes before Save in the DOM as on screen, so Tab reaches the
  safe choice first and Save is the submit button that Enter in a field
  presses.
- The icon-only ⋯ button is named "More actions".
- A Confirm Dialog focuses Cancel when it opens, so Enter cannot delete;
  with type to confirm, it focuses the field.
- The reference table names each row by its action (a row header), so a
  screen reader announces "Save" with each cell.

patterns-application-ui-container--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ContainerStories from './Container.stories'

<Meta of={ContainerStories} />

# Container

Caps a page's content at a maximum width and centres it in the space it
is given. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Layout: Containers.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/container.json
```

Container only sets a width. Inside an [App
Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs), [App
Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs) owns the
page: its padding, its scroll and the aside column. Put a Container inside
it when a page should not stretch across a wide screen, a settings page or
a form; leave it out for a table that uses every column.

## Sizes

`size` is the widest the content gets: `sm` 48rem for a form or a settings
page, `md` (the default) 64rem for most pages, `lg` 80rem for a wide table
or a dashboard.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Sizes} />

## Padded

`padded` adds side padding by breakpoint, for a page outside the App
Shell, such as a sign-in page or a public page: `--space-container`, and
`--space-section` from a 64rem viewport: App Content's tokens and step,
measured against the viewport instead of the shell, on the sides only.
The cap measures the content, so a padded and an unpadded Container of one
size give the same line length.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Padded} />

## In an App Shell

No `padded`: App Content already pads the page, and the Container centres
the content in it. With an aside, it centres in the page column.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.InAppShell} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ContainerStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Full width up to the cap.** It fills its parent, block, grid or flex,
  until it reaches its size, then centres with equal space on each side.
- **Narrower than its size,** it takes the width it is given and never
  overflows.
- **Padding follows the viewport,** not a container query: outside the
  App Shell no ancestor is a size container to query.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Containers, and where this departs from them:

- **Three steps, not every `max-w-*`.** `sm`, `md` and `lg` follow
  Tailwind's `max-w-3xl`, `5xl` and `7xl`.
- **Padding is opt-in and uses the kit's spacing tokens.** Tailwind pads
  every container (`px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`); here App Content pads the page
  in the shell, so padding twice would be wrong. One step at 64rem, as in
  App Content, instead of Tailwind's two.
- **No "full width on mobile" variant.** Under its size a Container is
  already full width; a flush, unpadded page on a phone is App Content's
  job.

## Accessibility

- A plain `div`: no landmark, no role and no focus. The landmark is the
  `main` around it (App Content's, or your own outside the shell).
- It changes no order; content reads and tabs in DOM order.
- At 320px it takes the full width and its content reflows; it adds no
  horizontal scroll.

patterns-application-ui-data-table-page-.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DataTablePageStories from './DataTablePage.stories'

<Meta of={DataTablePageStories} />

# Data Table Page

A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs),
what is shown and the pages below it, and, while rows are selected, what
you can do with them. Two pieces, `TableToolbar` (with
`TableToolbarGroup`) and `TableFooter`, around the kit's Table, Search,
Select and Pagination. Filtering, paging and the data are yours: the
stories show one way to wire them.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/data-table-page.json
```

## Toolbar and pagination

The footer holds a Pagination given `totalItems`, so it shows the rows on
screen ("6–10 of 12") and a "Rows per page" select from
`pageSizeOptions`. Any lone child spans the footer, so Pagination's summary
leads and the pages end the bar; the wrapping inside is Pagination's own.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.ToolbarAndPagination} />

## Bulk actions

With `selectedCount` above zero the toolbar swaps its tools for the
selection's actions and a "Clear selection" button, on the accent
surface so the change of mode is visible.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.BulkActions} />

## Empty result

When nothing matches, the Table's `emptyState` says so and offers the way
back; the footer goes away.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.EmptyResult} />

## Props

**TableToolbar**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | Search, filters, the primary action. |
| `selectedCount` | number | `0` | From 1, the selection bar replaces the children. |
| `selectionActions` | node | – | |
| `onClearSelection` | function | – | Shows "Clear selection". |
| `selectionLabel` | `(n) => string` | `"{n} selected"` | |

`TableToolbarGroup` wraps the part that should take the free space and
wrap first, usually the search and filters.

**TableFooter** takes, as children, usually a Pagination with `totalItems`
and `pageSizeOptions`. Its own `summary` slot is for a footer without
Pagination's summary, such as "12 projects" on a list that fits one page;
do not pass both, or the count is shown twice.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.FooterSummary} />

## Behaviour to copy

- **Rows per page keeps the reader in place.** Pagination moves to the page
  holding the first row that was on screen and reports it through
  `onPageChange`; keep `page` and `pageSize` in your state.
- **Filtering returns to page 1.** A new query on page 3 would otherwise
  show an empty page, or a page the reader never asked for.
- **Selection is by id**, so it survives sorting and paging (Table's
  `getRowId`), and an action clears it once it has been applied.

## Layout

- No breakpoints: both bars are flex rows that wrap, so they adapt to the
  width of their container, not the viewport.
- `TableToolbarGroup` grows from 16rem and wraps first. On a phone the
  search takes its own line and the filters and the primary action flow
  under it, instead of anything shrinking below use.
- In selection mode the actions are pushed to the end of the bar and drop
  under the count when they no longer fit.
- The footer puts the summary at the start and the pages and rows-per-page
  select at the end; when they do not fit, they wrap under the summary.

## Accessibility

- The selection count is a polite status line that is always in the page,
  so "2 selected" is announced as it changes, and silence when it clears.
- The footer's "6–10 of 12" is Pagination's own status line, inside the
  pages landmark ("Projects pages"), so a new page or page size is
  announced too.
- Search and the status filter are named ("Search projects", "Status")
  without visible labels, since the table's caption and placeholder make
  their purpose clear on screen.
- The empty state is a heading inside the table's body, so a screen reader
  reaching the table hears why it is empty.

patterns-application-ui-description-list.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DescriptionListStories from './DescriptionList.stories'

<Meta of={DescriptionListStories} />

# Description List

The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order,
an application. It is read-only; its editable twin is a settings form in
Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/description-list.json
```

## Columns

Term and details side by side, a line between rows, and an optional
action at the end of each row ("Update").

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## In a card

`isCard` puts the header in a top band and the list below it, inside one
border. With `layout="grid"`, fields run two to a row; `isWide` gives
long text and attachments the full width.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.InCard} />

## Stacked

Term over details, one field after another: for a sidebar or a narrow
panel.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Stacked} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DescriptionItem[]` | – | Required. `{ term, details, action?, isWide? }` |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons at the end of the header. |
| `layout` | `columns`, `grid`, `stacked` | `columns` | |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

<Controls of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## Layout

- **It responds to its own width, not the viewport's.** Columns and grid
  are container queries: under 36rem of list width they stack, so the
  same list works in a main column, a sidebar and a phone.

  <Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.ColumnsNarrow} />

- Details wrap anywhere, so a long email address or URL never pushes the
  layout wide.

## Accessibility

- A real `<dl>`: a screen reader announces a list of terms and reads each
  detail with its term.
- Row actions sit in their own `<dd>` after the details. Give each one the
  field it acts on ("Update Email address"), hidden if you like, so a
  list of links is not six identical "Update"s.

patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--.title: Patterns/Application UI/Event Calendar
patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as EventCalendarStories from './EventCalendar.stories'

<Meta of={EventCalendarStories} />

# Event Calendar

Events on a month, week, day or year view, with a header to move through
time and switch views: a team's schedule, bookings, deadlines. After
Tailwind UI Application UI, Data Display: Calendars.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar-events.json
```

It owns no events: pass the ones you have, and it shows those that fall in
view. Picking a date is the [Calendar](?path=/docs/data-display-calendar--docs)
component; this pattern reuses its date helpers, and draws the year view
with it.

## Month

The default view. Each day lists its events, all-day ones first, then by
start time with the time after the title. A day with more than three
lists two and "n more", which opens the day view (or picks the day for the
list below). An all-day or multi-day event shows on every day it covers.
`actions` takes the header's last slot, e.g. an "Add event" button.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Month} />

## Week

An hour grid, a column per day. Timed events sit by their start and end;
events that overlap share the width side by side. All-day events, and
timed events that cross midnight, go to a row above the hours. The grid
opens at the week's first timed event, or at 8:00.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Week} />

## Day

The week's hour grid, one column wide.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Day} />

## Year

Twelve small Calendars. Picking a day opens it in the day view (or the
month, when `views` leaves the day out).

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Year} />

## The selected day's events

`hasEventList` lists the selected day's events under the month, in full.
With `views={['month']}` the view switch is gone.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.WithEventList} />

## Clickable events

`onEventClick` makes events buttons, to open one in a
[Drawer](?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs) for example; an event with
`href` is a link.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Clickable} />

## Empty

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={EventCalendarStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through. Each event takes `id`,
`title`, `start`, and optionally `end` (exclusive for a timed event, the
last day for an all-day one), `allDay`, `color` (a Tag variant) and
`href`.

## Layout

- **The header wraps.** Title first; the arrows and Today, the view
  switch and `actions` follow on the same row while it has room, then
  drop under the title.
- **A month under 40rem wide shows dots, not titles**: one per event, up
  to three, in the event's colour. The day's button still says how many.
  Turn on `hasEventList` wherever the calendar can be that narrow, so the
  titles are one tap away. It follows the calendar's own width, not the
  viewport's.
- **The week keeps each day at least 6rem** and scrolls sideways under
  that; the day view takes the full width. Both show ten hours and scroll
  for the rest.
- **Long titles are cut with an ellipsis** in the month; in the hour grid
  they clip at the event's edge. The full title is in the event's
  accessible name either way.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Calendars, and where this departs from them:

- **The view switch is a Select**, as Tailwind's menu is, but it changes
  only the view: "Add event" is yours to put in `actions`.
- **Multi-day events repeat on each day** in the month, rather than one
  bar across the week. Simpler, and it reads the same on a phone.
- **The narrow week does not swap to a strip of days.** It scrolls
  sideways; pick the day view for a phone.
- **No "current time" line** in the week and day views.
- **The year view marks no events.** It is twelve Calendars, and Calendar
  has no way to mark a day; its API stays as it is. Pick a day to see it.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading (`headingLevel`, 2 by default) and a polite live
  region, so moving through time is announced. The event list's heading
  is one level below.
- The month is a table named by the title, with a column header per
  weekday. Each day is a button named by its full date and its number of
  events, `aria-pressed` when selected and `aria-current="date"` on today.
- One day is a tab stop. The arrow keys move the selected day (across the
  month's edge too, which turns the month) and focus follows; Tab goes
  on to that day's events. Right to left, left and right follow the
  screen.
- Events are links with `href`, buttons with `onEventClick`, and text
  otherwise. Their name is the title then the start time.
- In the week and day views each day is a list named by its full date,
  and the all-day row's lists say "All day". The hour labels and the day
  headings above the columns are hidden from assistive tech: the lists
  carry the dates and the events their times. The scrolling hours are a
  focusable group, so a keyboard can scroll them.
- Previous and Next are named for the view's unit ("Next week"); their
  arrows mirror right to left.

patterns-application-ui-feed--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FeedStories from './Feed.stories'

<Meta of={FeedStories} />

# Feed

What happened to a record, or across many, as a list of sentences: who
did what to what, and when, with what they wrote under it. For a
record's history, a comment thread, or recent activity on a home page.
After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: Feeds.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/feed.json
```

## Simple

An Icon per kind of event, joined by a line. Each event is one
sentence: `actor` in bold, then `action`, the rest of it, then the time.
Build the sentence so it reads whole: "changed the status of Harbor
Lights from Active to On hold", not "Status: Active → On hold".

<Canvas of={FeedStories.Simple} />

## With comments

An Avatar for an event a person made, an Icon for one the system made,
and what they wrote in a box under the sentence. The [Project
Detail](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-project-detail--docs)
template puts a status change's note there.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithComments} />

## Without the line

`hasConnector={false}` drops the line, for a short list where each event
stands alone.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithoutConnector} />

## With a comment box

`composer` takes a form and puts it after the last event, lined up with
the sentences. The form is yours: a labelled
[Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs) and a Button,
adding to the items you pass. A thread with a box lists oldest first,
so the newest sits by the box.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithComposer} />

## Linked and unread

`href` makes the sentence a link whose target is the whole row, and
`isUnread` ends the row with a dot; `onClick` runs when the link is
followed, to mark the item read. The [Notification
Center](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-notification-center--docs)
lists its notifications this way. With `href`, keep links out of
`actor` and `action`: links cannot nest.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.LinkedAndUnread} />

## Empty

No items shows `empty`, "No activity yet." by default, in place of the
list. The composer still shows, so the first comment can be written.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={FeedStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the
feed with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its
own.

## Layout

- The media column is as wide as a small Avatar; an Icon sits in a
  filled circle of that size, and an Avatar covers it.
- The line runs down the centre of that column, from one media to the
  next, and stops at the last.
- The time follows the sentence instead of taking a column at the end,
  so the feed fits a narrow aside: it wraps whole, never mid-date.
- Long names, links and comments break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Time** follows the sentence instead of sitting at the end of the
  row: the feed lives in asides and expanded rows as often as on a page.
- **Comment** is a slot of the event, not a separate event type, so any
  event can carry text: a status change keeps its reason.
- **Composer**: Tailwind draws the box with the user's avatar beside it.
  Here it lines up with the sentences and the form is yours.

## Accessibility

- The events are an ordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are and where each one sits.
- The media is hidden from assistive tech: the sentence names the
  person and the event, so the avatar or icon adds nothing to hear.
- Each time is a `<time>` element with the full ISO moment, whatever
  `formatTime` shows.
- The feed has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label` when it stands
  alone, as the Projects row does ("Harbor Lights activity").
- A row with `href` is one link, named by its sentence; the time and
  comment sit outside it.
- The unread dot is an image named "Unread", so the state is heard as
  well as seen.

patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FilterBarStories from './FilterBar.stories'

<Meta of={FilterBarStories} />

# Filter Bar

Search and filters above a list or table, with the filters in force shown
as chips that each remove on their own, and Clear all. After SAP Fiori List
Report (filter bar), Carbon Filtering and Polaris Index table.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/filter-bar.json
```

The pattern owns no data: it lays out the controls you pass and renders the
`applied` list you keep. Choose how each filter applies with the component
you put in `filters`.

## Applied at once

A button per field opens a [Menu](?path=/docs/navigation-menu--docs) of
checkbox items; each tick applies straight away and adds a chip. Use it for
the few fields people filter by most, with short lists of values.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Default} />

## Applied in a batch

More filters opens a [Drawer](?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs) holding a
draft: nothing changes until Apply, and Cancel drops the draft. Use it for
the long tail of fields, or when each change is slow to run (a server query
over a large ledger).

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.AppliedInABatch} />

## Empty

With nothing applied there is no chip row and no Clear all.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Empty} />

## In a table toolbar

Put it first inside a [TableToolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs):
it takes the free space, the page's main action stays at the end, and the
toolbar swaps it for the selection's actions while rows are selected.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.InTableToolbar} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={FilterBarStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Two rows.** The controls on top; the chips and Clear all under them,
  only while something is applied.
- **Everything wraps, nothing squeezes.** On a phone the search takes its
  own line and the field buttons flow under it; chips wrap onto more lines.
- **A long value truncates inside its chip** with an ellipsis, rather than
  widen the page. The remove button keeps the full name.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `search` landmark named "Filters"; pass `aria-label` to
  name it after what it filters, e.g. "Invoice filters", when a page has
  more than one.
- The chips are a list named "Applied filters", so a screen reader says how
  many are in force. Each remove button is named after its chip, e.g.
  "Remove Status: Overdue".
- Removing a chip moves focus to the chip that takes its place, or the one
  before; removing the last one, or Clear all, moves it to the first
  control, usually the search. Focus never drops to the page.
- Field buttons say only the field ("Status"); what is chosen is read from
  the chips and from the checked items in the menu.

patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--do.title: Patterns/Application UI/Form Layouts
patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FormLayoutsStories from './FormLayouts.stories'

<Meta of={FormLayoutsStories} />

# Form Layouts

How the kit's fields are arranged into a form: sections with a heading
and a line of context, fields one or two to a row, and a row of actions
at the end. Four pieces: `FormSection`, `FormFieldGroup`,
`FormFullWidth` and `FormActions`. The `<form>` element is yours.
After Tailwind UI's Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/form-layouts.json
```

## Settings sections

A settings page. Each section's title and description sit in a column
beside its fields, sections are separated by a line, and one row of
actions saves the lot.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.SettingsSections} />

## Stacked in a card

One section on a card: the title above, fields two to a row, and the
actions in the card's bottom band.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.StackedInCard} />

## Field groups

Related fields inside one section, under a legend: an address, a set of
checkboxes. `FormFieldGroup` is a `<fieldset>`: it takes the section's
whole row, lays out its own columns, and `disabled` turns off every field
in it, Checkbox, Switch and Radio included (they are left out of the
submitted data, as the browser does for any disabled field). Slider and
File Uploader do not read the group: give them `disabled` too. Disable a
group while it does not apply, with the reason on screen, as the "Ship to
the billing address" checkbox does here; see
[Field › Disabled](?path=/docs/components-inputs-field--docs) for when to
disable, hide or make read-only.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.FieldGroups} />

## In a modal

A short form in a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).
The submit button sits in the modal's footer, outside the `<form>`, and
points at it with the `form` attribute, so Enter in a field and a click on
the button both submit.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.InModal} />

## FormSection props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. An `h2` by default. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`. |
| `layout` | `split`, `stacked` | `split` | Split puts the intro in a column beside the fields. |
| `columns` | `1`, `2` | `1` | Two fields to a row. Wrap one in `FormFullWidth` to span the row. |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `footer` | node | – | Usually `FormActions`; the card's bottom band when `isCard`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

`FormFieldGroup` takes `legend` (required), `description`, `columns`
(`1`, `2`) and everything a `<fieldset>` takes, `disabled` among them.

`FormActions` is a row of buttons aligned to the end: secondary actions
first, the primary one last.

<Controls of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

## Layout

- **Sections respond to their own width.** Split turns into stacked under
  48rem of section width, and two columns into one when the fields' side
  of the section (its whole width once stacked) is under 32rem. A form in
  a sidebar or a phone needs no extra props.
- **Sections are size containers**, so they take their width from where
  they sit. As a flex or grid item that would shrink to fit, give the
  section a width (`inline-size: 100%`), or it collapses.

  <Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

- **A field group takes a whole row** of a two-column section, and its
  own `columns` follow the same 32rem rule.
- Labels sit above their fields, never beside them: the label width does
  not depend on the longest translation, and a form reflows to a phone
  with no change.
- Actions end-aligned, primary last: the same place in every form, where
  the eye and the Tab key end up.

## Accessibility

- Each section is a `<section>` with a heading, so the form's parts are in
  the page outline and a screen reader can jump between them.
- Group related fields in a `FormFieldGroup`, as the Notifications and
  Billing sections do: a `group` named by its legend and described by its
  description, so a screen reader announces both on entering it.
  RadioGroup is a group of its own; do not wrap it.
- Mark required fields with `required`. The field shows the asterisk and
  the browser enforces it; say in the description if most fields are
  optional instead.
- Never disable the submit button to show that a form is incomplete. Let
  it submit, and show what is missing next to each field.

patterns-application-ui-grid-list--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import * as GridListStories from './GridList.stories' # Grid List Records as cards in a grid: people on a team, projects, files and photos. Each card names the record, says a little about it, and either opens it or offers its actions. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: Grid Lists. ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/grid-list.json ``` A card takes the same item as a [Stacked List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs) row, plus an optional `cover`, so a list can switch between rows and cards without reshaping its data. Use cards when the picture or the record's identity matters more than comparing facts down a column; use Stacked List when people scan and compare. ## Simple An Avatar or an Icon, the `title` with a `description` under it, and `meta` under that: an email, an owner, a date. ## Linked `href` makes the title a link whose target is the whole card. `status` takes a Tag (or a Badge) and puts it after the title. ## With actions `actions` takes [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) entries, as in Stacked List and Table's `rowActions`: a ⋯ button in the card's corner, named "Actions for" the title, and a [Context Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-context-menu--docs) on the card with the same entries. A card with `href` keeps the browser's own link menu instead, so there the ⋯ button is the only way in. A card can link and have actions: the menu sits above the card's link, so a click on it opens the menu, not the record. Keep `status`, `description` and `meta` free of controls on a linked card: the link covers them. ## With a cover `cover` puts a picture across the top of the card, edge to edge, at 16:9: a file preview, a photo, a logo. It is decorative, so give the `` `alt=""`; the title names the card. ## Footer and empty The card panels, the footer and the empty state come from [List Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-list-container--docs), always in its `separate` appearance: a card is its own panel, so there is no `flat` or `card` grid. `footer` goes after the grid; `empty` shows in place of it, "Nothing here yet." by default. ## Props Every `
` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the grid with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its own. ## Layout - As many columns at least 16rem wide as the container fits, measured on the container rather than the viewport: three in 840px, one in a narrow aside or on a phone. There is no breakpoint of its own. - A lone card stays one column wide instead of stretching across the row. - Cards in a row are as tall as the tallest; text starts at the top. - Long titles, emails and paths break anywhere rather than overflow. ## Differences from the spec - **Column count** follows the container, not fixed counts per viewport breakpoint as in Tailwind, so the grid works in a side panel too. - **Actions** are a ⋯ Menu, not a row of buttons along the bottom of the card (Tailwind's contact cards with Email and Call): two or more actions fit one menu at every width, and the card stays one shape. - **Centred contact cards** (avatar above the name) are left out: one layout, media beside the title, reads the same as a Stacked List row. ## Accessibility - The cards are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many there are. Reading and tab order go left to right, then down. - The media and the cover are hidden from assistive tech: the title names the record. - A card with `href` is one link, named by its title; the status, description and meta sit outside it. - Each card is one tab stop, two with actions: the link, then the ⋯ button. - The ⋯ button is named "Actions for" the title; keep `title` a string when there are actions. The context menu is a shortcut to the same entries, never the only way to reach one. - The grid has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

patterns-application-ui-import-export--d.title: Patterns/Application UI/Import Export
patterns-application-ui-import-export--d.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ImportExportStories from './ImportExport.stories'

<Meta of={ImportExportStories} />

# Import Export

Getting rows into a list from a file, and out of it into one: the
spreadsheet round trip every ERP and back-office list needs. No outside
block covers it (Catalyst Blocks has none); the anatomy is the
Application UI catalogue's own. Two dialogs,
`ImportDialog` and `ExportDialog`, built from the [File
Uploader](?path=/docs/components-inputs-file-uploader--docs),
[Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs),
[Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs) and [Column
Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs) in a
[Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs). The
[Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs) index
page uses both.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/import-export.json
```

## Import

Three steps, then the result.

1. **Upload**: one file, CSV by default. `templateHref` links a blank
   file with the right headings.
2. **Map columns**: each column of the file goes into one of your
   `fields`, or is not imported. A heading that matches a field's key,
   label or one of its `aliases` is mapped already, so a file made from
   the template needs no work here. A field takes one column; Next waits
   until every required field has one.
3. **Review**: every row with its problems beside it, from `validate`
   and from required fields left empty. A row with a problem is skipped,
   not fixed here: the file is the place to fix it. The button says how
   many rows it imports.

The result says how many were imported and how many skipped, and offers
the skipped rows as a CSV, with their problems in a last column, to fix
and upload again.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Default} />

## Mapping

No heading matches a required field: the step names it and Next waits.
Choosing a field already taken moves it to this column.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.MapColumns} />

## Errors

A file that cannot be read, or has no rows, says so on the upload step.
An `onImport` that throws keeps you on the review step with its message:
nothing is lost, and Import can be tried again.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Errors} />

## Export

Which rows (`scopes`: all, the current view, the selection, each with its
count), which format when there is more than one, and which columns,
ticked from the ones on screen. Each opening starts from those defaults,
since the view or the selection may have changed. Export calls
`onExport` and closes. A long export returns at once and says when the
file is ready with a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs)
and a Download action, as the story does.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Export} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ImportExportStories} />

`ExportDialog` takes `scopes` (radio options), `defaultScope`, `formats`
(radio options; one format hides the choice, CSV by default), `columns`
and `defaultColumnKeys` (as the Column Chooser's), `onExport`, which gets
`{ format, scope, columns }` and may return a promise, and the same
`trigger`, `title`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `container`.

The pattern owns no data. Reading the file is `readFile` (CSV text by
default; for Excel, read it with your spreadsheet library into `{ columns,
rows }` and widen `accept`), checking a row is `validate`, saving is
`onImport`, and writing the export is `onExport`. Three helpers come
with it: `parseCsv`, `toCsv` and `downloadCsv`. `toCsv` puts a `'` before
a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` and is not a number, so a
spreadsheet shows it instead of running it as a formula.

## Layout

- The import is a large Modal (48rem), never wider than the window; the
  export a medium one.
- The review scrolls inside the dialog under its sticky heading row,
  so the summary above it and the buttons under it stay in view. It
  lists the first 100 rows and says how many more there are; the import
  still takes them all.
- Long values with no spaces break rather than widen the table.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.LongFile} />

## Differences from the spec

The catalogue lists Confirm as a step of its own. Here the review is the
confirmation: its button says how many rows it imports and the summary
above it how many it skips, so a fourth step would only repeat them.
Formats beyond CSV, and reading Excel, are the app's: the pattern adds no
spreadsheet library. The notice when an export is done is the app's
too, a Toast, since only the app knows when its file is ready. Both
dialogs are Modals rather than Drawers: each is a task that blocks the
list until it is done, not a side panel to keep open beside it.

## Accessibility

- Each dialog is named by its title. The import closes on Escape or its
  close button, not on a click outside, so a stray click does not throw
  away a mapped file.
- The steps are a navigation landmark, "Import steps", with the current
  step marked and each step's state said.
- Rows are numbered as a spreadsheet numbers them, the heading row
  being 1, so a problem can be found in the file. Blank rows keep their
  number and are not imported.
- Each mapping Select is named after its column: "Field for Budget".
- The review is a scrollable region the keyboard can reach and scroll.
  Each row's problems are text in its row, under a Problems heading, not
  colour alone.
- A failed read or import is announced as an alert; the result is
  announced as a status.
- The skipped rows and the template are real downloads, a button and a
  link.

patterns-application-ui-inline-edit--doc.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as InlineEditStories from './InlineEdit.stories'

<Meta of={InlineEditStories} />

# Inline Edit

A value that edits where it stands, in a table cell or a description list
row, so changing one field does not take a trip to a form. After the inline
edit of enterprise SaaS and ERP tools (Salesforce, Airtable, SAP Fiori's
editable tables).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-edit.json
```

The pattern owns no data. It shows `value`, calls `onSave` with the new
one, and shows the message you return when the save fails.

## Description list

Each detail of a record edits in its row. Hover or focus a value and a
pencil shows that it can change; click it, or press Enter on it, and it
becomes a text input with the whole value selected. Enter or Save keeps the
change, Escape or Cancel drops it.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Default} />

## Table cell

Put it in a column's `cell`. Use `size="sm"` in a table row, and name each
one by its row in `label` ("PO reference for INV-1041"), since every cell in
the column says the same thing otherwise.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.InTable} />

## Error

Return a message from `onSave` (or throw one) and it shows under the field,
which stays open with what was typed. Typing again clears it. Check the
format here: the input is always `type="text"`, so `inputMode` only picks
the on-screen keyboard.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Invalid} />

## Saving

Return a promise and the field is saving until it settles: the input is
read-only, Save spins, and Cancel and Escape wait. A rejection shows its
message as an error.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Saving} />

## Leaving the field

Tab or click away and the change is saved, not lost. Focus goes where the
viewer sent it, and a slow save does not pull it back. A save that fails
leaves the field open with its error. An unchanged value closes without calling `onSave`.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.SaveOnBlur} />

## Empty and long values

An empty value shows `placeholder`, muted, so there is still something to
click. A long value wraps, even with no spaces, instead of widening the
cell.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.EmptyAndLong} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={InlineEditStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through to the root.

## Layout

- **The value lines up with the text around it.** The root pulls back by
  the field's inline padding, so the value's text starts where a plain
  cell's text does, and the input's text starts in the same place: entering
  edit mode does not shift it. It pulls back by the extra height too, so the
  value sits on the same line as the term or the cells beside it.
- **Save and Cancel sit at the end of the input**, aligned to its box; an
  error goes under the box and pushes the row taller, not the buttons down.
- **The pencil does not take space away from the value** on hover: it has
  its place from the start, hidden until hover or focus. On a touch screen,
  where nothing hovers, it always shows.
- **On a touch screen** the value's hit area grows to 44px without the value
  growing.

## Accessibility

- The value is a button named "Edit {label}: {value}", so a screen reader
  says what it edits and what it holds. Enter or Space on it opens the
  input, focused, with the value selected.
- The input is named by `label`. Enter saves; Escape cancels and does not
  close a Drawer or Modal around it.
- After Enter, Save, Escape or Cancel, focus returns to the value.
- An error marks the input invalid and becomes its description, so it is
  read with the field; a status announces it too, since after a blur save
  focus has already left.
- While saving, a status says "Saving" and Save is busy. Escape waits,
  and still does not reach the overlay.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Keyboard} />

patterns-application-ui-list-container--.title: Patterns/Application UI/List Container
patterns-application-ui-list-container--.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ListContainerStories from './ListContainer.stories'

<Meta of={ListContainerStories} />

# List Container

The frame around a list: a line between rows, optionally a panel around
them, a footer and an empty state. It owns the rows' padding and dividers
and nothing inside them. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: List
containers.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/list-container.json
```

`ListContainer` is the `<ul>` and its frame; `ListContainerItem` is one
`<li>`, padded as a Table row. For records (an avatar, a title, a status, a
link or actions), use [Stacked
List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs): it renders
through List Container and takes the same `appearance`, `footer` and
`empty`, so there is one way to frame a list, add a footer or say it is
empty.

## Flat

Rows divided by a line, no frame. The default: a list in a page section,
or in a panel that already has an edge.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Flat} />

## Card

The same rows in a bordered panel, as an outline Card, for a list that
stands on its own on the page.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Card} />

## Separate

Each row its own panel, a gap instead of lines: rows that read as separate
objects rather than one list.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Separate} />

## With Stacked List

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.WithStackedList} />

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.SeparateStackedList} />

## Empty

No rows shows `empty`, "Nothing here yet." by default, in place of the
list, inside the frame. The footer still shows.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ListContainerStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, and every `<li>`
attribute to `ListContainerItem`.

## Layout

- Rows pad by `--space-inline` above and below and `--space-4` at the
  sides, and are at least `--row-height` tall, so a list lines up with a
  Table of the same density.
- `footer` sits past a divider in `flat` and `card`, and after the gap in
  `separate`.
- No breakpoints: the container is as wide as its column. Long words in a
  row break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Full width on mobile** (Tailwind's card and separate variants that
  drop their side edges on small screens) is left out: whether a panel
  bleeds to the screen edge is the page layout's call, not the list's.
- **Flat card** (a tinted panel without a border) is the `card`
  appearance: one panel look, the outline Card's.

## Accessibility

- The rows are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are. Keep `ListContainerItem` the only child of the container, so
  the list has only `<li>` children.
- The empty state is a paragraph in place of the list, so an empty list
  is not announced as a list of zero items.
- The container has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

patterns-application-ui-media-object--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import * as MediaObjectStories from './MediaObject.stories' # Media Object Media beside a block of text: an avatar by a comment, an icon by a setting, a thumbnail by a product. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Layout: Media Objects. ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/media-object.json ``` Use it for one thing on its own. A list of records is a [Stacked List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs) or a [Grid List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-grid-list--docs); a history of events is a [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs); the top row of a card is a [Card Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs). Those lay out their own media because each treats it differently (a filled circle, a timeline, a heading-sized row). A framed block with a picture on the side is a [Card](?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs) with `orientation="horizontal"`. ## Basic `media`, then `title` and `description`. The title is bold text, so a column of comments does not fill the page outline with headings. ## As a heading `headingLevel` makes the title a heading, for a media object that starts a section. ## Alignment `align` places the media at the top (the default), the middle or the bottom of the text, or stretches it to the text's height. ## Media at the end `mediaPosition="end"` draws the media after the text. The DOM order does not change. ## Nested `children` comes after the description: actions, or a reply as another Media Object, which lines up with the parent's text. ## Props Every other `
` attribute passes through. ## Layout - **No breakpoint.** Media and text share a row while the text keeps 12rem; in a narrower container the text wraps under the media. It follows the container, so it works in an aside as on a full page. - **Long words break anywhere** rather than overflow. ## Differences from the spec Tailwind UI's Media Objects, and where this departs from them: - **Responsive stacking follows the container, not the viewport.** The text wraps under the media only when it would get less than 12rem, so an avatar stays beside its text on a phone. Tailwind's "basic responsive" and "wide responsive" stack below the `sm` breakpoint, and the wide one swaps a large image's size; neither is a separate variant here. - **Stretch suits a thumbnail or a placeholder** with no fixed height. An Avatar or an `` with a height keeps it. - **The media is always decorative**, and `headingLevel` is opt-in; Tailwind uses an `h4` every time. ## Accessibility - The media is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title says who or what it is. Do not put a link or a button in `media`. - The title is a paragraph unless `headingLevel` is set. Set it only when the object starts a section, and pick the level that follows the heading above, so the outline has no gaps. - `mediaPosition="end"` moves the media visually only (CSS `order`); reading and focus order stay media, title, description, then `children`.

patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--doc.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as NavSidebarStories from './NavSidebar.stories' # Nav Sidebar The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen, laid out as in the Claude apps: the logo and the collapse button on top, a header for the tenant switcher and search, links in categories, and a footer for the account, notifications and help. It can collapse to an icon rail. A pattern, one of the three pieces the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places (with the Top Bar and App Content); it was the Navigation/Sidebar component. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Expanded | The default: icon, label and badge on every row. | | Collapsible (`isCollapsible`) | Apps where the content needs the width at times: a button in the top row folds the sidebar to the rail. | | Rail (`isCollapsed` or `defaultCollapsed`) | Icons only, labels in tooltips. For tools the reader knows well. The header and footer stay, as icons; items without an icon are left out. | | Plain | No logo, header or footer: a section's own navigation inside a larger layout. | ### Rail preview Collapsed, resting the mouse on the rail for a moment floats the full sidebar over the page, as in the Claude apps; the rail keeps its place in the layout, so the page does not move. The preview's top button, "Keep sidebar open", docks it. It stays while a menu opened from it is open. Touch and keyboard do not open it: keyboard focus reaches the same links in the rail, and the expand button docks the sidebar. ### Categories A group is a category. `isCollapsible` makes its label a button that opens and closes it; `limit` shows its first items with a small "Show more" for the rest, and the current page is never hidden behind the limit. `action` is opt-in: a button at the end of the label row (an icon Button that adds an item, say), shown on hover and focus. Leave it off where nothing is added from the sidebar. ### Header and footer rows `NavSidebarButton` is a row that looks like an item: an icon, a label, an optional `badge`, `description` line and `end` (a chevron, a shortcut). It is a button, so it can be a Menu's or Popover's trigger. Its appearances: | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `ghost` | A row like an item: notifications (with its count as `badge`), help, the account. | | `switcher` | A tenant or workspace switcher: the name in medium weight, its chevron right after it, the avatar a rounded square. | | `field` | A search button drawn as an input, its shortcut hint at the far end, that opens a command palette. | An Avatar in the leading slot is 20px in every density, and every leading visual (logo mark, avatar, icon) is centred on the nav icons' line. In the rail a row shows its icon only and takes its label (and badge) as its name and tooltip. ### Backgrounds Gray is the sidebar's own `--surface-filled`, and what a transparent sidebar shows on the neutral canvas. In an App Shell it can also be white (`sidebarSurface="solid"`, the current item in the brand tint) or transparent on a deep canvas of your own; see Sidebar surfaces on the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) page. ## Resources Copied into your project through the registry, like every pattern (not in the npm package): ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/nav-sidebar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx) - Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it - Behaviour: a plain `
`; the rail's labels use [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy In the rail the logo keeps its place, cut to the rail's width, and the expand button shows over it on hover or focus. The header and footer stay as icons; labels, badges, category heads and "Show more" are hidden, and each category starts with a rule instead of its label. ## Measurements Items are rows of the md control tier, 2px apart in every density, so hover and current fills never touch. Expanded, the sidebar is 16rem wide. The rail is one square row plus the padding either side: `--control-md` plus twice `--space-2`. A long label is cut with an ellipsis. Give the sidebar the height to fill; its body scrolls when the items do not fit. ## Color Hover is an overlay, not a solid: in dark mode the sidebar's own surface is the same grey as `--accent`, so an opaque hover fill would vanish. A badge is a count that needs attention, so it is red and sits right after its label. An App Shell overrides the current fill, the hover, the search field and the badge for its white and transparent surfaces. ## States }, ]} > - **Current** is a `--selected` fill, a step past the hover fill so the two never read alike, plus medium weight for anyone who cannot tell the fills apart. It stays off the accent: where you are is not a call to action. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the row, so rows that sit flush do not cover each other's ring. - **Collapsed** is the rail; see Variants. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through. ## When to use Use a NavSidebar for an app's main navigation when it has more than five or so destinations, or will grow: the list runs down and does not wrap. Name groups by what is in them, keep labels to a word or two, and give every item an icon if the sidebar can collapse. } doCaption="Short labels, an icon on each, grouped under a few names." dont={} dontCaption="Long labels get cut, and with no icons there is nothing to show in the rail." /> ## When not to use - **For three to five sections of one page or object.** Use [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs) across the top. - **For actions.** A sidebar goes places. Put actions in [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) or a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs). - **On a phone, as is.** 16rem is most of a phone's width. In an [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) under 64rem it is always the icon rail, with no collapse button; elsewhere, pass `isCollapsed`. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Main"; rename it with `aria-label` when the page has another navigation. The current item has `aria-current="page"`. - Each group's label names its list through `aria-labelledby` ("Projects, list, 3 items"), and keeps doing so in the rail, where it is only visually hidden. Labels are not headings, so they do not compete with the page's outline. - In the rail each link keeps its name through `aria-label`, badge included ("Inbox, 12"), and a tooltip shows the same text on hover and on keyboard focus. - The collapse button is named "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar" and carries `aria-expanded`; in the rail preview it is "Keep sidebar open". - A badge joins its row's name after a comma ("Inbox, 12", "Notifications, 3"), expanded and in the rail alike. - The rail preview opens on mouse hover only. Keyboard focus never covers the rail with it: the rail's links are reachable as they are, and the expand button docks the sidebar. - A collapsible category's label is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at its list; Enter and Space open and close it. A category's `action` needs its own name ("Add to Pinned"). - A `NavSidebarButton` is named by its text; in the rail, by its `label` through `aria-label`, with the same text as a tooltip. - Rows are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).

patterns-application-ui-notification-cen.title: Patterns/Application UI/Notification Center
patterns-application-ui-notification-cen.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as NotificationCenterStories from './NotificationCenter.stories'

<Meta of={NotificationCenterStories} />

# Notification Center

What needs your attention across the app: a bell in the [Top
Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs) with the unread
count on it, and a panel under it listing the notifications, newest
first, unread ones marked with a dot. After Catalyst Blocks,
Notifications.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/notification-center.json
```

## In the Top Bar

`NotificationCenter` is the bell and the panel. The bell is a ghost icon
Button with a floating [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs)
for the unread count, and opens the panel in a
[Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). The rows are a
[Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) without the
connecting line: each is a sentence, `href` makes the whole row a link,
and `isUnread` puts a dot at its end and counts it.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Open} />

## With tabs

`hasTabs` adds All and Unread tabs; Unread carries the count, and shows
`emptyUnread` once everything is read. `NotificationPanel` is the inside
on its own, for a [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-overlays-drawer--docs)
or a column of a page.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.WithTabs} />

## Empty

No items shows `empty` in place of the list; the bell has no count and
Mark all as read is disabled.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={NotificationCenterStories} />

`NotificationPanel` takes the same props except `label`, `side`, `align`,
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `container`, which belong to
the bell and its Popover. The pattern owns no data: `onMarkAllRead` is
where you set every `isUnread` to false, and an item's `onClick` runs
when its link is followed, to mark that one read.

A notification that arrives while the panel is closed only changes the
count. When it needs attention now, also raise a
[Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): the count is
not announced, and the bell is easy to miss.

## Layout

- The panel is as wide as a Popover goes (22rem), and narrower when the
  window is.
- It is no taller than the room under the bell. The list scrolls; the
  header stays pinned at the top.
- The header wraps: the actions drop under the heading when they do
  not fit beside it.
- The unread dot has a column of its own at the end of the row, so the
  sentence never runs under it. Long names and file names break anywhere
  rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Settings** is not a built-in button: `actions` takes what the app
  has, such as a More menu with View all and Notification settings.
- **Tabs** are optional; a short list reads fine without them.
- **Time** is the Feed's: pass a relative `formatTime` ("5 minutes ago")
  as the stories do.

## Accessibility

- The bell's name carries the count ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the
  floating badge is hidden, so the count is said once.
- The panel is a dialog named "Notifications". Opening it moves focus
  inside; Escape closes it and returns focus to the bell.
- A heading (level 2 by default, `headingLevel` to change it) names the
  panel for heading navigation.
- The notifications are a list. A row with `href` is one link: the
  sentence is its text, and the whole row is its target.
- An unread row ends with a dot named "Unread", so the state is heard
  as well as seen.
- Mark all as read is disabled when nothing is unread.

patterns-application-ui-saved-views--doc.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SavedViewsStories from './SavedViews.stories'

<Meta of={SavedViewsStories} />

# Saved Views

The views of a list or table, the ones that ship with the product and the
ones people save, with a mark when the view in force has changed, Save,
Save as new view and Manage views. After SAP Fiori variant management
(List Report, Worklist) and Polaris Index filters.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/saved-views.json
```

The pattern owns no views: it renders the `views` you keep and calls you
back. What a view holds (filters, sort, columns) is yours to store; compare
it with what is on screen and pass `isModified`. Picking another view puts
that view's saved state in force and drops unsaved changes, as in Fiori:
Modified, beside the views, is the warning.

## Tabs

For a handful of views. Each tab can carry a count. Put it above a
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs): picking
a view puts its filters in force there.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Default} />

## Modified

Change a filter and the view says Modified, with Discard and Save. Save
writes the change into the view in force.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Modified} />

## Save as new view

A predefined view cannot be saved over, so a change offers Save as new view
in place of Save; it is also always in View actions. The dialog asks for a
name, refuses an empty or taken one, and with `isShareable` offers to share
the view.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.SaveAsNewView} />

## Manage views

In View actions when you pass `onDelete`. It lists every view, marks the
predefined and shared ones, and deletes saved ones at once: pair it with an
Undo toast if a view is costly to rebuild. Deleting the view in force is
yours to handle: put another view in force, usually the first. There is no
rename or unshare yet: save a copy under the new name, then delete the old
one.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.ManageViews} />

## Menu

For more views than fit on one line: a button names the view in force and
opens the views as a menu.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.AsMenu} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SavedViewsStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **One row** while there is room: the views take the free space, the
  actions sit at the end.
- **The actions drop under the views** when the row is too narrow, rather
  than squeeze the tabs.
- **More tabs than fit scroll sideways** inside the bar; nothing widens the
  page. Past five or six views, use `display="menu"`.
- In menu display a long view name truncates with an ellipsis.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- In tabs display the views are a tab list named "Views" (Manage views'
  list takes the same name); pass
  `aria-label` to say what they list, e.g. "Invoice views". Each tab's name
  includes its count.
- In menu display the button's name says the list and the view in force,
  e.g. "Invoice views: All"; the views are radio items in the menu.
- Modified sits in a `status` region, so a screen reader announces it when
  a change makes the view differ from what is saved.
- Save as new view moves focus to the name field. A missing or taken name
  marks the field invalid and names the problem in its description.
- Manage views: each delete button is named after its view, e.g. "Delete
  To chase". Deleting one moves focus to the next delete button, or the one
  before, or to Done when none is left.
- Save, Discard and Save as new view take away the button that was
  pressed; focus moves to the view in force.

patterns-application-ui-session--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SessionStories from './Session.stories'
import { SessionTimeout } from './Session'

<Meta of={SessionStories} />

# Session

The two ends of a session: **Session Timeout**, the warning a minute
before an idle session ends, and **Signed Out**, the page the reader lands
on after it ends, with the account they were signed in to and **Sign in
again**. After Carbon's login pattern. Built on
[Modal](?path=/docs/overlays-modal--docs) (as an alert dialog), the **Auth
Layout** (see [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)),
Button and Link.

Neither part knows about sessions. The app tracks inactivity, opens the
warning, extends or ends the session from its buttons, and picks the
reason the signed-out page gives.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/session.json
```

## Session timeout warning

Open it `countdown` seconds (60 by default) before an idle session ends.
The time left counts down in the sentence. **Stay signed in** has focus,
since that is what most readers want; it and Escape call `onContinue`,
where you extend the session and close the warning. **Sign out** calls
`onSignOut`. At zero, `onExpire` (or `onSignOut` when you leave it out):
sign out and show Signed Out with reason `inactive`.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Warning} />

Keep `countdown` at 20 seconds or more: WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable)
asks for a warning and at least 20 seconds to extend with a simple action.
The countdown runs to a fixed end, so a background tab, whose timers the
browser slows down, still ends on time. Closing and reopening it starts
the count again.

## Signed out

The page after a session ends, with a title and a line for the `reason`:

- `signed-out` (default): the reader pressed Sign out.
- `inactive`: the warning ran out.
- `expired`: the server ended the session, for example a token reached
  its lifetime.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.SignedOutPage} />

### Remembered account

Pass `account` (an email or a username, masked if you need to) to say which
account **Sign in again** is for, and carry it in `signInHref` so the reader
only types a password: [Progressive Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-progressive-sign-in--docs)
takes it as `defaultEmail`, which is also where its **Remember my email**
comes back. `otherAccountHref` adds **Use another account**. Leave
`account` out after a deliberate sign out on a shared computer.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Inactive} />

## Props

### Signed Out

<ArgTypes of={SessionStories} />

Every other Auth Layout prop (`brand`, `appearance`, `aside`, `footer`) and
`<div>` attribute passes through.

### Session Timeout

<ArgTypes of={SessionTimeout} />

## Layout

- **Session Timeout** is a small (24rem) modal, never wider than the
  screen. The buttons sit at the end of the footer, Stay signed in last.
- **Signed Out** follows the Auth Layout: one 25rem column centred on the
  canvas, in a card by default. A long account breaks anywhere instead of
  pushing the page sideways at 320px.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The warning is an `alertdialog` named by its title and described by its
  sentence, so a screen reader reads the time left once, when it opens.
  The time is a `timer`, which is not a live region: it does not announce
  every second.
- Focus moves to **Stay signed in** when the warning opens, and back to
  where it was when it closes. Enter keeps the session; Escape does too.
- Signed Out has one `h1`, the reason, inside `main`. **Sign in again** is
  the first control in the page, before Use another account.

patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StackedListStories from './StackedList.stories'

<Meta of={StackedListStories} />

# Stacked List

Records as rows, one under the other: people on a team, projects, files,
invoices. Each row names the record, says a little about it, and either
opens it or offers its actions. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists:
Stacked Lists; Polaris Resource list; Salesforce Item.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stacked-list.json
```

## Simple

An Avatar or an Icon, the `title` with a `description` under it, and
`meta` at the end: facts that help pick the row out, such as a role, an
owner or a date. A line divides the rows.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Simple} />

## Linked

`href` makes the title a link whose target is the whole row, with a
chevron at the end to say it opens. `status` takes a Tag (or a Badge)
and puts it after the title.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Linked} />

## With actions

`actions` takes [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)
entries, the same as Table's `rowActions`: a ⋯ button at the end of the
row, named "Actions for" the title, and a [Context
Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-context-menu--docs) on the row
with the same entries, for right click or long press. A row with `href`
keeps the browser's own link menu instead (open in a new tab, copy the
link), so there the ⋯ button is the only way in.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithActions} />

A row can link and have actions: the menu takes the chevron's place and
sits above the row's link, so a click on it opens the menu, not the
record. Keep `status`, `description` and `meta` free of controls on a
linked row: the row's link covers them.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.LinkedWithActions} />

## Frame, footer and empty

The frame, the lines between rows, the footer and the empty state come
from [List Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-list-container--docs):
`appearance` puts the list in a card (`card`) or makes each row its own
panel (`separate`).

`footer` goes after the last row, past a divider. A list on its own page
takes a [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs);
a short list in a card or on a dashboard takes a "View all" link.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithPagination} />

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithViewAll} />

### Empty

No items shows `empty`, "Nothing here yet." by default, in place of the
list. The footer still shows.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={StackedListStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the
list with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its
own.

## Layout

- The media column is as wide as a medium Avatar; an Icon sits in a
  filled circle of that size, and an Avatar covers it.
- `meta` sits at the end of the row while the title fits beside it, and
  wraps under the text when it does not. The list has no breakpoint of
  its own, so it works in a narrow aside as on a full page.
- Long titles, emails and paths break anywhere rather than overflow.
- Rows pad by `--space-inline` above and below, as Table rows do, and
  are at least `--row-height` tall: a one-line row without media lines up
  with a Table row of the same density.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Selection and bulk actions** (Polaris) are left out: a list you
  select from and act on in bulk is a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).
- **Actions** are a ⋯ Menu, not buttons written out in the row:
  Tailwind's "View" button is the row link, and two or more actions fit
  one menu at every width.
- **Meta** wraps under the text instead of hiding on small screens, so
  nothing is lost on a phone.

## Accessibility

- The rows are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are.
- The media is hidden from assistive tech: the title names the record.
- A row with `href` is one link, named by its title; the status,
  description and meta sit outside it. The chevron is decorative.
- Each row is one tab stop, two with actions: the link, then the ⋯
  button.
- The ⋯ button is named "Actions for" the title; keep `title` a string
  when there are actions, or it falls back to "Actions for item 2". The
  context menu is a shortcut to the same entries, never the only way to
  reach one.
- The list has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

patterns-application-ui-stats--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StatsStories from './Stats.stories'

<Meta of={StatsStories} />

# Stats

Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and
optionally how it moved since the last period, an icon, and a link to
the details. The top of a dashboard or a report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stats.json
```

## Simple

<Canvas of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## With trend

`previous` gives the figure to compare against; `change` says by how
much and which way. The colour follows whether the change is good news,
not its direction: pass `isPositive: true` for figures where down is
good, like churn or response time.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithTrend} />

## With icon and link

An icon on a rounded square of the primary colour, and a link at the foot of each
card to where the figure comes from.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithIconAndLink} />

## With sparkline

A trend at the foot of each card, edge to edge: pass a `Sparkline` as the
stat's `chart`. Leave out the spark where the period has no data and the
card would only say "No data" twice.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithSparkline} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `Stat[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `title` | node | – | A heading above the cards. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

Each `Stat` has `label`, `value`, and optionally `previous`, `change`
(`{ value, direction: 'up' \| 'down', isPositive? }`), `icon`, `href`,
`linkLabel` (default "View all") and `chart` (a node at the foot of the card,
usually a `Sparkline`).

<Controls of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- As many 14rem columns as fit: three or four on a desktop, one on a
  phone. Cards in a row share a height.

  <Canvas of={StatsStories.Narrow} />

- Figures use tabular numbers, so a row of values lines up digit by digit
  and does not jitter when it updates.

## Accessibility

- A definition list: each figure is the definition of its label, so a
  screen reader reads "Total subscribers, 71,897".
- The change is read as words ("Increased by 12%"), not only shown as an
  arrow and a colour. The colours are `--success-text` and `--danger-text`
  on their subtle surfaces, 4.5:1 in both appearances.
- Each "View all" link carries its figure's label for screen readers
  ("View all Avg. open rate"), so a list of links is not three identical
  entries.
- The icon is decorative.
- The sparkline is decorative too (`aria-hidden`): the change already says
  the trend in words.
