patterns-application-ui-table-chart-swit.title: Patterns/Application UI/Table Chart Switch
patterns-application-ui-table-chart-swit.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TableChartSwitchStories from './TableChartSwitch.stories'

<Meta of={TableChartSwitchStories} />

# Table Chart Switch

One set of records, two ways to look at it: a table of the rows and a chart
of their totals, under the same filters. After the table/chart toggle of
SAP Fiori's List Report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table-chart.json
```

The pattern owns no data and draws neither view: it lays out the filters,
the summary and the switch, and shows the view in force. Filter once and
hand the same result to both `table` and `chart`, so the two never disagree.

## Table and chart

The table comes first. Switch to the chart and the filters stay where they
are, with their state; a change shows in whichever view is in force. The
view not in force is hidden, not removed, so the table keeps its sort,
selection and scroll while the viewer looks at the chart.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Default} />

The chart keeps its own View as table. That table lists what the chart
plots (a total per month), not the records, so the two do not overlap.

## Controlled

Pass `view` and `onViewChange` to bring a viewer back to the view they left,
or to keep it in a [Saved View](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-saved-views--docs).

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Controlled} />

## Empty

Nothing matches: each view shows its own empty state, the Table's
`emptyState` and the chart's No data.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Empty} />

## Differences from the spec

- Fiori's toggle is a pair of icon buttons in the table toolbar; here it is
  a pair of text tabs, since the views are panels of one region and a word
  says more than a glyph.
- A `summary` slot, Fiori's "Invoices (128)" beside the toggle, gives the
  row a start and the count a voice.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={TableChartSwitchStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Filters on top**, full width.
- **The summary and the switch share a row** below them: the summary at the
  start, the switch at the end, where Fiori puts it in the table's toolbar.
- **The view takes the full width** under that row. A wide table scrolls
  inside its own box.
- **When the row is too narrow** the summary wraps and the switch drops
  under it; nothing widens the page.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The switch is a tab list named "View"; pass `aria-label` to say what it
  shows, e.g. "Invoice view". The view in force is its tab panel, named
  after its tab.
- The summary is a `status`: when a filter changes the count, a screen
  reader announces it.
- Arrow keys move between Table and Chart, Enter or Space switches, and
  focus stays on the tab.
- The filters stay in the page when the view changes, so focus in them is
  never lost.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Keyboard} />

patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TopBarStories from './TopBar.stories'

<Meta of={TopBarStories} />

# Top Bar

The bar above the page: `start`, a middle and `end` slots, and `TopBarNav`
for navigation links across it. One of the three pieces the
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places; inside
one it also shows the shell's `brand`. It was `AppHeader` (and
`TopBarNav` was `AppNav`).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/top-bar.json
```

## Search and actions

<Canvas of={TopBarStories.Default} />

## Top navigation

`TopBarNav` takes `items` (`{ label, href }[]`) and `currentHref`. Links
that do not fit scroll sideways, so on a phone they stay in the bar.

<Canvas of={TopBarStories.WithNavigation} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | node | – | Breadcrumbs, or TopBarNav links. |
| `children` | node | – | The middle, e.g. a wide search field. |
| `end` | node | – | Search, notifications, the account menu. |

## Layout

- The bar is one row, `--control-md` plus two `--space-cluster` tall, so
  it follows density. Its fill and edge come from the App Shell's top cell
  (solid or transparent), not from the bar.
- In the shell's top-bar layout with a sidebar, the brand takes a cell as
  wide as the sidebar (`--sidebar-width`), so the logo sits where it sits
  in the sidebar layout.
- Breakpoints read the container, which in an app is the shell.

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `header`; inside an App Shell it is the page's banner.
- `TopBarNav` is a `nav` named "Main"; the current page has
  `aria-current="page"` and is shown by more than colour.

patterns-application-ui-vertical-nav--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as VerticalNavStories from './VerticalNav.stories'

<Meta of={VerticalNavStories} />

# Vertical Nav

Secondary navigation inside a page: the sections of Settings, or the
parts of a long record, as a column of links beside the content. The
app's own navigation is the [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs);
this one has no rail, no collapse and no fill, and sits on the page.
After Tailwind UI Application UI, Navigation: Vertical navigation.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/vertical-nav.json
```

## With icons

An icon before each label helps when the reader comes back often and
scans by shape. Use icons on every item or on none. A count after the
label is information (how many members), so it is a secondary
[Badge](?path=/docs/atomic-elements-badge--docs), not the Nav Sidebar's
red one for unread items.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.WithIcons} />

## Grouped

Past seven or so sections, name groups of them. Ungrouped items before
the first group form a list of their own.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.Grouped} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={VerticalNavStories} />

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **No width of its own.** It fills the column the page gives it; the
  page decides the column's width and what happens on a narrow screen
  (the Settings template stacks it above the content).
- **Long labels wrap** rather than truncate: a cut-off section name hides
  which section it is. A word with no spaces breaks anywhere.
- Rows are `--control-md` tall at least, as in the Nav Sidebar, and
  `--target-coarse` under a coarse pointer.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.LongLabels} />

## Accessibility

- It is a `nav` landmark and needs an `aria-label` ("Settings"): the
  app's own navigation is already a navigation landmark, so the two need
  different names.
- The current section has `aria-current="page"` as well as the selected
  fill and medium weight, so it is not shown by color alone.
- A group label names its list ("Workspace, list, 4 items") and is not a
  heading, so it cannot break the page's heading outline.
- A count joins the link's name after a comma ("Members, 12").
  Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive tech.
- Tab moves down the links in order; there are no other stops.

templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AppShellStories from './AppShell.stories'

<Meta of={AppShellStories} />

# App Shell

A template: the frame of an application. It only places three patterns,
the [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs) (`TopBar`,
with `TopBarNav` for links across it), the
[Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs)
(`NavSidebar`) and the
[App Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs)
(`AppContent`, which the shell puts around its children), on the Theme's
canvas, with no padding or gap of its own. The navigation stays put while
the page scrolls, and on a phone the sidebar narrows to its icon rail.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-shell.json
```

## Sidebar layout

The default, `layout="sidebar"`: the sidebar runs the full height and
there is **no top bar** on wide screens. What a top bar would hold goes in
the NavSidebar, laid out as in the Claude apps: the logo and the collapse
button in its top row, the tenant switcher and search in its `header`,
notifications, help and the account in its `footer`. Below 64rem the
sidebar is the rail: its header and footer rows stay, as icons, and the
header comes back above the page with the logo.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithSidebar} />

## Top bar layout

`layout="top-bar"`: the header runs the full width above the sidebar and
the page.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopBarLayout} />

## The logo

Pass the logo as `brand`, not inside the NavSidebar or the TopBar. The
shell places it in the same spot in both layouts: its left edge on the
sidebar icons' left edge, centred in a row as tall as the top bar. It does
not move when the sidebar collapses, and it follows density. In the
sidebar layout the shell hands it to the NavSidebar's top row, next to the
collapse button; a collapsed rail cuts the logo to the rail's width, so lead
the logo with its mark. It is rendered once, wherever it shows. A sidebar
that is not a NavSidebar gets no logo in the sidebar layout.

## Canvas and content style

Two settings on the `Theme`, so a
whole app takes them at once:

- **`canvas`**: what the shell sits on. `plain` (the card colour),
  `neutral` (the page gray, the default) or `tinted` (the accent's subtle
  step). For any other colour or a gradient, pass
  `tokens={{ canvas, 'canvas-solid', 'canvas-foreground', 'canvas-muted-foreground' }}`,
  where `canvas-solid` is one colour standing for the canvas (for a
  gradient, a colour from its middle): components on the canvas use it as
  the surface under them, for a Badge's ring or a Checkbox's fill.
  The kit checks contrast for its own three canvases only; a custom canvas,
  in light and in dark (use `var(--use-light, …) var(--use-dark, …)`), is
  yours to check.
- **`contentStyle`**: how the page meets the canvas. `flat` (the default)
  puts it on one card surface, inset 8px from the edges at every density
  and flush below 48rem. `card` leaves it on the canvas, and each block is
  a [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) with
  `appearance="surface"`, which is raised under `card` and a ruled-off
  section under `flat`.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.CardOnTint} />

Each piece of the shell is `solid` (the card colour, with an edge where it
meets the page) or `transparent` (the canvas, its text in the canvas
colours): `topBarSurface` (default `solid`) and `sidebarSurface` (default
`transparent`). On a `plain` canvas a transparent piece keeps its edge,
since nothing else marks it. That edge keys off `canvas="plain"`: with a
custom canvas from `tokens`, set `canvas` to the preset closest to it
(`plain` for a white one) so the edges follow.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TransparentOnPlain} />

### Sidebar surfaces

The NavSidebar takes each surface's colours from the shell:

- **Gray**: `transparent` on the `neutral` canvas, the sidebar's own look.
- **White**: `solid`. The current item takes the brand's light tint
  (`--primary-subtle`), since a gray fill on white reads as hover.
- **Transparent on a deep canvas of your own**: a colour or gradient dark
  enough for white text. Beside `canvas`, `canvas-solid`, `canvas-foreground`
  and `canvas-muted-foreground`, the Theme tokens `canvas-hover`,
  `canvas-selected`, `canvas-field`, `canvas-field-border`, `canvas-badge`
  and `canvas-badge-foreground` set the sidebar's fills on it. Dark veils
  (black at 12–24%) for hover, the current item and the search field deepen
  the canvas under white text; a white badge with red text stands out on
  any hue, a red canvas included. On a canvas of the brand's own hue, give
  a brand avatar the `subtle` variant, or it vanishes.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.SidebarSurfaces} />

## Combinations

Of the 36 combinations of layout, the two surfaces, canvas and content
style, 24 occur in real products. The other 12 render but should not be
used:

- no `plain` canvas with `flat` content;
- no `transparent` top bar over a `solid` sidebar (on a `plain` canvas it
  looks the same as a solid one, so that case is fine);
- no `solid` full-height sidebar (`layout="sidebar"`) with `flat` content.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.Combinations} />

## Collapsed rail

NavSidebar's `isCollapsible` turns it into an icon rail that the reader can
expand. The links keep their names, and show them as tooltips; the header
and footer stay, as icons.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.CollapsedRail} />

## Top navigation

No sidebar: a logo and `TopBarNav` links in the header. On a phone the
links stay in the bar and scroll sideways when they do not fit.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopNavigationMobile} />

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopNavigation} />

## With an aside

Three columns, after Tailwind UI's multi-column layouts: the sidebar, the
page and an `aside` on the right for what supports the page, such as a
summary, a status or recent activity. Pass it as `aside`, and name it with
`asideLabel`. From 80rem of shell width it sits beside the page, as wide as
the expanded sidebar (`--sidebar-width`), and each column scrolls on its
own, so the summary stays in view while the page scrolls. It takes the
page's surface: a second card under `flat`, the canvas under `card`.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithAside} />

Under 80rem there is no room for a third column next to a usable page, so
the aside follows the page and the two scroll as one. Nothing is hidden,
but the aside now comes after the whole page, so keep what the reader
needs first in the page itself.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithAsideStacked} />

## On a phone

Under 64rem of shell width the sidebar stays beside the page as the icon
rail, and cannot expand: 16rem would cover most of a phone. The links keep
their names, as tooltips. There is no menu button and no drawer.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.Mobile} />

## Props

**AppShell**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `sidebar`, `top-bar` | `sidebar` | Full-height sidebar with no top bar, or a full-width top bar. |
| `topBarSurface` | `solid`, `transparent` | `solid` | The header on the card colour or on the canvas. |
| `sidebarSurface` | `solid`, `transparent` | `transparent` | The sidebar on the card colour or on the canvas. |
| `brand` | node | – | The logo, placed by the shell. |
| `sidebar` | node | – | A NavSidebar. Beside the content at every width; the icon rail below 64rem. |
| `header` | node | – | A TopBar. In `sidebar` it shows only below 64rem; without one the shell adds a plain TopBar there for the logo. |
| `aside` | node | – | A column beside the page, in an `aside` landmark. Right of the page from 80rem, below it under 80rem. |
| `asideLabel` | string | – | The aside's accessible name. |
| `mainId` | string | generated | The `id` of the `main` element, the skip link's target. |
| `children` | node | – | The page, inside `<main>`. |

`sidebar={isAdmin && <NavSidebar … />}` works: `false` and `null` count as
no sidebar, so there is no empty column.

**TopBar** takes `start` (breadcrumbs, or a logo and TopBarNav), `end`
(search, notifications, the account menu) and `children` for the middle.

**TopBarNav** takes `items` (`{ label, href }[]`) and `currentHref`.

## Layout

- **The shell fills the viewport** (`block-size: 100dvh`) and only the
  page scrolls, so the sidebar and the header stay in place. Set
  `block-size` on it to put it in a smaller box.
- **The sidebar sits beside the page at every width.** From 64rem, in
  `layout="sidebar"`, it runs the full height and the top bar is hidden,
  because the sidebar holds what the bar would. Below 64rem it is the icon
  rail and the top bar comes back in both layouts, for the logo, search and
  the account.
- **An aside** sits right of the page from 80rem, `--sidebar-width` wide,
  and the page and the aside each scroll on their own. Under 80rem it goes
  below the page and the two scroll together; below 48rem it is flush too,
  ruled off from a flat page at the top.
- **Below 48rem** a flat page drops its 8px inset, edge and rounding and
  goes flush, since a frame around it only costs width on a phone.
- **Everything follows density**: the top bar is `--control-md` plus two
  `--space-cluster` tall, the sidebar is `--sidebar-width` wide, the page
  padding is `--space-section`. The 8px inset of a flat page does not
  change.
- **Breakpoints are the shell's own width**, which in an app is the
  viewport's. That is also what lets the stories show the phone layout in
  a 390px box.
- **The shell is a size container** (`container-type: inline-size`), so
  it takes its width from where it sits, never from its content. In a
  block it fills the line as usual; as a flex or grid item that would
  otherwise shrink to fit, give it a width (`inline-size: 100%` or
  `flex: 1`), or it collapses.

## Accessibility

- A "Skip to content" link is the first thing in the shell, visible when
  focused. It moves focus past the navigation to the `main` element. Give
  `mainId` when something else should link there too; otherwise the id is
  generated, so two shells in one page (as in these docs) never share it.
- The page is the `main` landmark; the sidebar and TopBarNav are `nav`
  landmarks named "Main".
- The aside is a `complementary` landmark, after the page in reading and
  focus order. Name it with `asideLabel`. It takes focus (`tabIndex={0}`)
  with a visible ring, so a keyboard can scroll it when it scrolls on its
  own and holds nothing focusable.
- In the rail each link keeps its name, so the navigation reads the same
  on a phone.
- The current page is marked `aria-current="page"` in both kinds of
  navigation, and shown by more than colour.

templates-application-ui-home--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as HomeStories from './Home.stories'

<Meta of={HomeStories} />

# Home

The page an app opens on: a greeting and the period to look at, a setup
guide while the workspace is new, the key figures, a chart and the user's
tasks in a grid of cards, and recent activity in the aside. After Tailwind
UI's home screens, shadcn's dashboard-01, Polaris' homepage and Fiori's
overview page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs),
[Stats](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stats--docs),
[Card Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs),
[Action Panel](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-action-panel--docs),
the charts and the kit's Select, Checkbox, Progress Bar and Card. The data
is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/home-template.json
```

<Canvas of={HomeStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Period**: Last 7, 30 or 90 days. It changes the figures that add up
  over time (hours logged, invoiced: each against the period before) and
  the chart. Active projects is a count as it stands now, so the period
  does not touch it; it links to the list instead.
- **Setup guide**: an Action Panel with the steps, how many are done and
  one button, for the next step. It shows until every step is done, then
  goes, and focus moves to the page's heading. It sits first, above the
  figures: while a workspace is new, setting it up is the job, and the
  figures are mostly empty anyway.
- **Your tasks**: what is assigned to you, soonest first, each with its
  project and when it is due; overdue says so in words as well as red.
  Ticking one keeps it in the list, struck through, so a slip can be undone.
  No tasks shows "Nothing due".
- **Recent activity**: the newest events across every project, each
  naming its project, in the aside: it is context, not the job, so it
  takes the side column on a desktop and goes under the page on a phone.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.SetupGuide} />

## Make it yours

`Home` reads the samples in `home-data.ts` and the Projects template's
`projects-data.ts`. Load your figures, tasks and setup steps in their
place, and pass `today={new Date()}`: the sample pins today so the page
and its tests hold still. `onTaskChange(id, isDone)` and
`onSetupStep(id)` are where your API calls go.

Keep the figures few, three or four, and only ones the reader acts on.
A card per figure the business tracks turns home into a report nobody
reads; put those in a report page and link to it. A card on home answers
"what needs me today?" or "is anything off?".

The recent activity list is the [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern, fed the same events
as the Project Detail template's.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.NothingDue} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={HomeStories} />

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- The greeting and the period share a row while there is room; the period
  drops under the greeting when there is not.
- The figures take as many columns as fit, one on a phone.
- From 40rem of page width the chart and the tasks sit side by side, the
  chart the wider; below, the tasks go under the chart. 40rem is less than
  a desktop page keeps with the sidebar and the aside both open.
- The aside is beside the page from 80rem of the shell's width, under it
  below that.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, the greeting; the cards' and the aside's titles are `h2`.
- The figures are a region named after the period ("Key figures, last
  30 days"), so the name changes with it.
- Each task is a checkbox named by its title and described by its project
  and when it is due ("Overdue", "Due today"), so the colour is never the
  only cue.
- The setup guide is a group named "Finish setting up"; its progress bar
  says how many steps are done, and a done step reads "(done)". When the
  last step is done the guide goes and focus moves to the `h1`, not to the
  page's body.
- The aside is a complementary landmark named "Recent activity".

templates-application-ui-settings--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SettingsStories from './Settings.stories'

<Meta of={SettingsStories} />

# Settings

The signed-in user's settings: a heading, a
[Vertical Nav](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-vertical-nav--docs) of
sections beside the one shown, each section a form of
[Form Sections](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)
with a save bar at its end, and a danger zone last. After Tailwind UI's
settings screens and Polaris' settings page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) and the
kit's Text Input, Textarea,
[Password Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-passwordinput--docs),
Checkbox, Radio, Modal and Button. The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/settings-template.json
```

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Nav**: Profile, Account and Notifications. A link swaps the section in
  place and becomes the current page. Every section stays mounted while
  hidden, so a half-done edit survives a look at another section.
- **Save bar**: at the end of each section's form, Discard and Save, with
  a status line. It sticks to the bottom of the view while a long form
  runs past the fold. Save stores what the form sends and says "Saved.";
  Discard puts the fields back to what was last saved. Both are always
  there: a disabled Save cannot say why it is disabled.
- **Account**: change password asks for the current password, to prove
  it is you, and a new one with its rules. Both are checked on send, focus
  goes to the first one to fix, and the fields empty once it changes.
- **Read-only**: the email is managed by the organisation's sign-in, so
  it is a read-only field that says who can change it, not a disabled one:
  it stays readable, focusable and sent with the form.
- **Danger zone**: Delete account, last on the Account section and set
  off by a rule, opens a [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs)
  that waits until the username is typed. Cancel or Escape keeps everything.

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Account} />

## Make it yours

`Settings` keeps the saved values in state and hands each save to
`onSave(section, values)`, the form's fields by name. Call your API there,
and load your values in place of the samples. Add a section by adding it
to `SECTIONS` and a `SectionForm` for it; past seven or so sections, group
them in the nav.

Settings are edited as forms with one Save per section, not field by
field with [Inline Edit](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-inline-edit--docs):
a reader changes several related values at once and expects to review them
before they apply. Inline edit suits a record read more than edited.
[Form Layouts' Settings Sections](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)
shows the sections alone; this template is the whole page around them.

The sample swaps sections in place. In an app with a router, give each nav
item its own URL (a `render` link), and render the section the URL names.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SettingsStories} />

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- From 48rem of page width the nav is a column as wide as the app's
  sidebar and stays in view while the section scrolls. Below that it
  stacks above the section, every link still showing: a settings nav is a
  handful of links, and folding it into a menu would hide where else to go.
- Form Sections split (title and description beside the fields) from
  48rem of their own width, and stack below.

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, "Settings"; each Form Section's title is an `h2`.
- The nav is a navigation landmark named "Settings", the shown section's
  link `aria-current="page"`. Focus stays on the link; the section follows
  it in reading order.
- Each section is a form named after it ("Profile", "Change password").
  The save bar's status line is a `status` live region, so "Saved." is
  announced without moving focus.
- A field that fails is marked `aria-invalid`, its message part of its
  description, and gets focus.
- Delete account opens an `alertdialog` named "Delete your account?",
  with focus in the field to type the username; the delete button stays
  disabled until it matches. On close focus returns to the button.

templates-auth-forgot-password--docs.title: Templates/Auth/Forgot Password
templates-auth-forgot-password--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ForgotPasswordStories from './ForgotPassword.stories'
import * as ResetPasswordStories from './ResetPassword.stories'

<Meta of={ForgotPasswordStories} />

# Forgot Password

Two pages for a forgotten password. **Forgot Password** asks for the
email, then says to check it. **Reset Password** is the page the emailed
link opens: a new password with its rules, then "Password changed". After
Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), the
`PasswordInput` Sign Up uses, and the kit's TextInput, Link, Alert and
Button.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/forgot-password-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Step 1, the email**: one field and Send reset link. An empty or
  malformed email is marked with a message and keeps focus. The email,
  trimmed, goes to `onRequest`.
- **Step 2, check your email**: "If an account exists for …, we sent it a
  link". It never says whether one does, so the page cannot be used to
  find out who has an account. Focus moves to the new title.
- **Resend link**: disabled for `resendCooldown` seconds (30 by default),
  showing the time left, then sends to the same email and says so. A
  failed resend shows why and starts no cooldown. It is the same button
  as OTP Input's Resend code.
- **No single sign-on buttons**: an account that signs in with a provider
  has no password here to reset.
- **Use a different email** goes back to step 1 with the email filled in.
- **Step 3, a new password** (Reset Password): the rules are listed under
  the field and ticked off as the reader types, at least 12 characters by
  default, as on Sign Up; pass your own `passwordRules`. There is no
  "confirm password" field: Show lets the reader check what they typed.
  Pass `email` to name the account and to let a password manager save the
  new password under it.
- **Password changed**: the form gives way to the title, a line and a Sign
  in button; focus moves to the title.
- **When it fails**: `onRequest` and `onChangePassword` return (or resolve
  to) a message, such as too many requests or an expired link. It shows
  above the form and is announced. If they throw or reject, the page says
  "Something went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Sent} />

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.LinkExpired} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's.

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.WithoutEmail} />

## Make it yours

`onRequest` calls your API, which emails a link with a single-use token
when the account exists and does nothing when it does not; return a
message only for what the reader can act on (too many requests). Mount
`ResetPassword` on the page the link opens, read the token from the URL,
and send it with the password in `onChangePassword`; return a message
when the token is expired or used. A code instead of a link? Build step 2
with OTP Input, which has the same resend button.

## Props

### ForgotPassword

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onRequest` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email }`, from the form and from Resend link. A returned message shows above the form and keeps the step; the button is busy while a promise is pending. |
| `resendCooldown` | seconds | `30` | Before Resend link is allowed, after each send. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Back to sign in" goes. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the Back to sign in link, outside the card. |

### ResetPassword

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | `string` | | The account the link is for: named under the title and given to password managers. |
| `passwordRules` | `{ label, test(password) }[]` | at least 12 characters | Listed under the password and ticked off; all must pass to send. |
| `onChangePassword` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ password }` once the rules pass. A returned message shows above the form; otherwise the page says the password changed. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Back to sign in" and Sign in go. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the form, outside the card. |

The title and the line under it change with the step, so neither takes
`title` or `description`. Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
A long email wraps; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- When a step replaces the form (Check your email, Password changed), focus
  moves to the new `h1`, so a screen reader reads the page from there and
  focus is not left on a button that is gone. Use a different email puts
  focus back in the email field.
- An invalid field has `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its
  description, and gets focus.
- Resend link is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the time
  left. After a resend, "We sent another link" is a `status`, announced
  politely, and focus moves to the `h1` because the button is disabled
  again.
- The password rules are the field's description, each followed by "(met)"
  or "(not met)". The message from `onRequest` or `onChangePassword` is an
  `alert`, and the button is `aria-busy` while it waits.
- The email for password managers is a `hidden` input: out of the tab order
  and the accessibility tree.

templates-auth-mfa-challenge--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MFAChallengeStories from './MFAChallenge.stories'

<Meta of={MFAChallengeStories} />

# MFA Challenge

The second step of signing in: the reader enters a one-time code from
their authenticator app, or the one sent to their phone or email. **Try
another way** switches method, and a **backup code** gets them in when
none is at hand. After Carbon's login pattern and shadcn's Input OTP.
Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), **OTP
Input** with its Resend code, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link,
Alert and Button.

Show it after the password, from **Sign In** or **Progressive Sign In**,
when the account has a second factor. Setting one up (the QR code, the
first backup codes) is a separate screen.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/mfa-challenge-template.json
```

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.Default} />

## What works

- **The code**: six cells by default (`codeLength`). Typing or pasting the
  last digit sends the form; **Verify** does too, and with cells empty it
  marks the field and says what is missing. `onVerify` gets the method's
  `id`, the code and **Remember this device**.
- **Where the code went**: the line under the title follows the method.
  An authenticator app: "Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator
  app." A text message or an email: "We sent a 6-digit code to •••• 4821",
  with the destination as you pass it (mask it yourself), and **Resend
  code** under the cells, counting down from `resendCooldown` seconds,
  calling `onResend` and saying the new code went out.
- **Try another way**, when the account has more than one method: the
  other methods ("Authenticator app", "Text message to •••• 4821", "Email
  to a•••@example.com") and **Back**. Picking one calls `onMethodSelect`,
  where you send its code, then shows its code step. A resend still on its
  way when the reader moves on is ignored.
- **Use a backup code**: a plain text field, since backup codes are longer
  and often have letters and a dash. `onVerify` gets it as method
  `'backup'`, trimmed. **Use a verification code instead** goes back.
- **Remember this device for 30 days**: the template stores nothing. When
  `rememberDevice` is true, set your trusted-device cookie for
  `rememberDeviceDays`, and skip this page next time.
- **When it fails**: every handler returns (or resolves to) a message. It
  shows above the form and is announced; a wrong code is cleared and the
  first cell focused. If a handler throws or rejects, the page says
  "Something went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.TextMessage} />

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.TryAnotherWay} />

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.BackupCode} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's. With one method and
`hasBackupCode={false}`, there are no other ways in to offer.

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.OnlyOneWay} />

## Make it yours

Pass the account's methods in the order you want, the default (the one
the reader set up first, or used last) first. Rate-limit `onVerify`,
`onResend` and `onMethodSelect` on the server and return the message
("Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."): the page shows it as it
is. After `onVerify` succeeds, navigate on.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `methods` | `{ id, kind: 'app' }` or `{ id, kind: 'sms' \| 'email', destination }`, in an array | | The account's second factors; the first shows first. |
| `onVerify` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ method, code, rememberDevice }`; `method` is an `id` or `'backup'`. A returned message shows above the form. |
| `onResend` | `(method) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Resend code, for `sms` and `email`. |
| `onMethodSelect` | `(method) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | A method picked under Try another way. A returned message keeps the list. |
| `codeLength` | `number` | `6` | Digits in a code. |
| `resendCooldown` | `number` | `30` | Seconds before Resend code is allowed. |
| `hasRememberDevice` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Remember this device. |
| `rememberDeviceDays` | `number` | `30` | The days in its label. |
| `hasBackupCode` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Use a backup code. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Back to sign in, under the form. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under Back to sign in, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
On a phone the six cells fit the column, and Try another way and Use a
backup code wrap onto two lines when they must.

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- The cells are a group named "Verification code"; the first cell has
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so the phone offers a code from a text
  message.
- An incomplete code marks the cells `aria-invalid="true"`, describes the
  group with the message and focuses the first cell; an empty backup code
  does the same on its field.
- Each step replaces the last, so focus moves on: to the first cell, to
  the backup code field, or to the new `h1` on the list of methods.
- A message from a handler is an `alert`, the "new code sent" note a
  `status`, and Verify is `aria-busy` while it waits.

import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProgressiveSignInStories from './ProgressiveSignIn.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressiveSignInStories} />

# Progressive Sign In

A sign-in page that asks for the email first and only then decides how
the account signs in: accounts whose organization uses single sign-on go
to their identity provider, the rest are asked for a password. After
Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), its
`PasswordInput` and `AuthProviders`, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox,
Spinner, Link, Alert and Button.

Use it when some of your customers sign in through their company's
identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace): they never see a
password field they cannot use. Where everyone signs in with a password,
use **Sign In**, which asks for both at once.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progressive-sign-in-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Step 1, the email**: one field, **Remember my email** and Continue. An
  empty or malformed email is marked with a message and keeps focus. The
  email, trimmed, goes to `onContinue`, which returns the route.
- **The route is yours**: `onContinue` looks the account up (by the
  domain, say) and returns nothing for a password, `{ sso: 'Okta' }` for
  single sign-on, or a message such as "This account is locked".
- **Step 2, a password**: "Signing in as …" with **Change**, the password
  with Show / Hide, Forgot password? and Sign in. Focus moves to the
  password. The email is also in a hidden field, so a password manager
  fills and saves the right account. `onSignIn` gets the email, Remember
  my email and the password.
- **Step 2, single sign-on**: the title says where the reader is going,
  with a spinner and the email, while your redirect loads. **Use a
  different email** goes back; it cannot stop a redirect that is already
  loading, so it is for when the provider does not answer.
- **Change** and **Use a different email** go back to step 1 with the email
  filled in and focused.
- **Remember my email**: the template does not store anything. Store the
  email when `rememberEmail` is true and pass it back as `defaultEmail`;
  the field then starts filled in and the box ticked.
- **Social buttons**: `providers` puts them above the email on step 1, as
  on Sign In. They are for consumer identities (Google, Microsoft), not a
  company's single sign-on, which the email routes to.
- **When it fails**: `onContinue` and `onSignIn` return (or resolve to) a
  message. It shows above the form and is announced; a wrong password is
  cleared and focused. If they throw or reject, the page says "Something
  went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Password} />

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.SingleSignOn} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's.

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.WithProviders} />

## Make it yours

`onContinue` calls your API with the email, which answers with the
account's sign-in method; for single sign-on, start the redirect (to
your identity provider's authorize URL) and return `{ sso }` with its
name for the page to show. Answer the same for an email with no account
as for one with a password, so the page cannot be used to find out who
has an account: the wrong password message then covers both. After
`onSignIn` succeeds, navigate on, or show a second factor.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onContinue` | `(values) => string \| void \| { sso } \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, rememberEmail }`. Nothing: the password step. `{ sso: name }`: the single sign-on step. A string: a message above the form. |
| `onSignIn` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, rememberEmail, password }`. A returned message shows above the form. |
| `defaultEmail` | `string` | | A remembered email: fills the field and ticks Remember my email. |
| `hasRememberEmail` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Remember my email. |
| `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | `[]` | Social buttons above the email, with an "or" line. |
| `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | Called with the button's `id`. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `"Sign in to your account"` | The `h1` of the email and password steps. |
| `forgotPasswordHref` | `string` | `"#forgot-password"` | On the password step. |
| `signUpHref` | `string` | | Shows "No account? Sign up". Leave it out where accounts are by invitation. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the form, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
A long email wraps, and Change drops under it; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- Continue replaces the email with the next step, so focus moves on: to
  the password, or to the new `h1` on the single sign-on step, where the
  spinner's "Taking you to …" is a `status`. Change and Use a different
  email put focus back in the email field.
- Change is named "Change email".
- An invalid field has `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its
  description, and gets focus.
- The message from `onContinue` or `onSignIn` is an `alert`, and the button
  is `aria-busy` while it waits.
- The email for password managers is a `hidden` input: out of the tab order
  and the accessibility tree.

templates-auth-sign-in--docs.content: import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import * as SignInStories from './SignIn.stories' # Sign In A sign-in page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have them, then email and password. After Tailwind UI's sign-in screens, shadcn/ui's login blocks and Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout**, the frame the other auth screens (sign up, reset password, multi-factor) share, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link, Alert and Button. ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/sign-in-template.json ``` ## What works - **Single sign-on**: a full-width button per provider, then an "or" line, then the form. `onProviderSelect` gets the provider's `id`; send the reader to your identity provider from there. - **Email and password**: Show reveals the password and turns into Hide; sending the form hides it again, so the browser does not keep it as plain text. The fields carry `autocomplete="username"` and `"current-password"`, so password managers fill them. - **Checks before sending**: an empty field, or an email with no `@`, is marked with a message saying what to do, and the first one gets focus. Typing in a field clears its message. Valid values go to `onSignIn`. - **Wrong credentials**: `onSignIn` returns (or resolves to) a message. It shows above the form and is announced, the password is cleared and focused, the email kept. Say "The email or password is incorrect", not which one: naming it tells an attacker which emails have accounts. If `onSignIn` throws or rejects, the page says "Something went wrong. Try again." instead. - **Keep me signed in**, **Forgot password?** and **Sign up** are links and a checkbox; drop the checkbox with `hasRememberMe={false}` and the link with no `signUpHref`. ## Variants **Card** (default): the form in a card on the Theme's canvas. The most common in business software; it reads as a step apart from the app. **Plain**: the form straight on the canvas, for a quieter page or a canvas that is already a colour or an image. Here also without single sign-on, Keep me signed in or sign-up, as where accounts come by invitation. **With a panel**: `aside` puts a panel beside the form from 64rem of the page's width: a picture, a customer quote, what is new. The form keeps the left half and lines up at its start. ## Make it yours Replace `onSignIn` with a call to your API and return its error message; on success, navigate away. `providers` takes `{ id, label, icon }`: the label is the whole button text ("Continue with Google", "Sign in with SSO"), the icon the provider's mark. The kit ships no brand marks. ## Props | Prop | Values | Default | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `title` | `ReactNode` | "Sign in to your account" | The page's `h1`. | | `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | none | Single sign-on and social buttons above the form. | | `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | A provider's button was pressed. | | `onSignIn` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, password, remember }` once the fields pass. A returned message shows above the form; the button is busy while a promise is pending. | | `hasRememberMe` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows "Keep me signed in". | | `forgotPasswordHref` | `string` | `"#forgot-password"` | Where "Forgot password?" goes. | | `signUpHref` | `string` | none | Shows "No account? Sign up". | | `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the sign-up line, outside the card: legal links, "Ask your administrator". | Every other Auth Layout prop below passes through; `children` is the page's form. ## Auth Layout `AuthLayout` (in `AuthLayout.tsx`) is the frame: the logo, an `h1`, an optional line under it, the form and a footer, in one column about 25rem wide, centred on the canvas. Every auth screen uses it, so they line up with each other. It owns no state. The same file exports `AuthDivider`, the "or" line. The password field with Show / Hide is the kit's [Password Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-passwordinput--docs) (pass `autoComplete="new-password"` where the password is being chosen; its button is named after a text `label`, "Show confirm password", so two on one page differ). ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/auth-layout.json ``` | Prop | Values | Default | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `brand` | `ReactNode` | | The logo, above the title. | | `title` | `ReactNode` | required | The page's `h1`. | | `description` | `ReactNode` | | A line under the title. | | `appearance` | `card`, `plain` | `card` | The form in a card, or straight on the canvas. templates-auth-sign-up--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SignUpStories from './SignUp.stories'

<Meta of={SignUpStories} />

# Sign Up

A sign-up page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have
them, then full name, email and a new password with its rules, the terms
and a link back to sign in. After shadcn/ui's sign-up blocks and Carbon's
login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)) and the
kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link, Alert and Button.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/sign-up-template.json
```

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Single sign-on**: as on Sign In, a full-width button per provider,
  then an "or" line, then the form. `onProviderSelect` gets the `id`.
- **One name field**, "Full name", not first and last: names do not split
  the same way everywhere. `autocomplete="name"` and `"email"` let the
  browser fill them.
- **A new password with its rules**: the rules are listed under the field
  from the start and ticked off as the reader types. The default is one
  rule, at least 12 characters, with no rules about kinds of characters
  (after NIST SP 800-63B); pass your own `passwordRules`. There is no
  "confirm password" field: Show lets the reader check what they typed.
  `autocomplete="new-password"` lets a password manager suggest one.
- **Terms**: pass `terms`, the label with its links, and a checkbox the
  reader must tick appears above the button. Leave it out and there is
  none; put a line in `footer` instead if your terms need no consent.
- **Checks before sending**: an empty field, an email with no `@`, an unmet
  rule or unticked terms is marked with a message saying what to do, and
  the first one gets focus. Typing clears a field's message. Valid values
  go to `onSignUp`.
- **The account cannot be made**: `onSignUp` returns (or resolves to) a
  message. It shows above the form and is announced; what was typed stays.
  If `onSignUp` throws or rejects, the page says "Something went wrong. Try
  again."

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.EmailTaken} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's. Plain here is also
without single sign-on or terms, the fewest parts.

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Plain} />

## Make it yours

Replace `onSignUp` with a call to your API and return its error message;
on success, send the reader on (to verify their email, or into the app).
Whether to say "An account with this email already exists" is your call:
it tells anyone which emails have accounts. Where that matters, accept
the sign-up and email the address instead.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | "Create your account" | The page's `h1`. |
| `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | none | Single sign-on and social buttons above the form. |
| `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | A provider's button was pressed. |
| `passwordRules` | `{ label, test(password) }[]` | at least 12 characters | Listed under the password and ticked off; all must pass to send. |
| `terms` | `ReactNode` | none | The label of a checkbox the reader must tick. |
| `onSignUp` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ name, email, password, acceptedTerms }` once the fields pass. A returned message shows above the form; the button is busy while a promise is pending. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Already have an account? Sign in" goes. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the sign-in line, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through. The rules come from
`PasswordInput`'s `rules` prop, so a reset-password page can list the same
ones.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout):
a column about 25rem wide in the middle of the page, the full width less
the padding on a phone, and a panel beside it from 64rem with `aside`. A
long title, rule or terms label wraps; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- Every field has a visible label. An invalid field has
  `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its description, and the first
  invalid field gets focus.
- The password rules are the field's description, each followed by
  "(met)" or "(not met)" for a screen reader, so they are read with the
  field. Ticking one off is not announced as you type; the tick and the
  colour show it on screen.
- The message from `onSignUp` is an `alert`, so it is announced. The
  Create account button is `aria-busy` while it waits, a second press
  sends nothing, and the single sign-on buttons are disabled.
- The terms checkbox's links are inside its label; pressing a link opens
  it, pressing the rest of the label ticks the box.

import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProjectDetailStories from './ProjectDetail.stories'

<Meta of={ProjectDetailStories} />

# Project Detail

An object page: one project, with a breadcrumb back to the list, a header
with its name, status, key facts and actions, tabs for its sections, and
an aside with its summary and activity. After Tailwind UI's detail
screens, Polaris' details page and Fiori's object page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) (its
`aside` column), [Description List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-description-list--docs)
and the kit's Breadcrumbs, Tabs, Table, Menu, Drawer, Tag and Button. It
is the record behind a row of [Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs).
The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/project-detail-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Breadcrumb**: Projects, then this project as the current page.
- **Header**: the name as the `h1`, the status tag beside it, and the key
  facts under it: PM, timeline, and the team's head count. Edit and a "More actions" menu
  (Archive or Restore) sit at its end.
- **Tabs**: Overview (PM, timeline, estimation) and Team (who works on it, in
  a table).
- **Aside**: the summary (status, health, last update) and
  the activity, newest first, on the [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern: the same list a
  Projects row expands to.
- **Edit** opens a Drawer with the name, status and estimation. Save
  updates the page, and a status or estimation change joins the top of
  the activity. Cancel, Escape or the close button drops the edit; a
  press on the backdrop does nothing, so a stray click loses nothing. An
  empty name is refused.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Edit} />

## Make it yours

`ProjectDetail` takes `project` (a `Project`, see `projects-data.ts`) and
`team` (`TeamMember[]`), and keeps the project in state. Replace the
samples with your data, and the `setProject` calls (Save, Archive) with
calls to your API. Add a tab per section of your record; a long record that reads top
to bottom can drop the tabs and stack its sections instead.

There is no save bar: the page is for reading, and editing happens in the
drawer, which owns its Save and Cancel. A record edited in place, field
by field, is the job of inline edit, not this page.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `Project` | the first sample project | The record. Read once; later changes are local. |
| `team` | `TeamMember[]` | `sampleTeam` | The Team tab's rows. Empty shows an empty state. |

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- From 80rem of shell width the aside sits right of the page and each
  scrolls on its own, so the summary stays in view; under 80rem it
  follows the page and the two scroll as one (App Shell). Keep what the
  reader needs first in the page, not the aside.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Stacked} />

- The header's actions share the name's row while there is room and drop
  under it when there is not. The status tag wraps under a long name, and
  the key facts wrap one by one.
- A long name with no spaces wraps, in the header and the breadcrumb;
  the page never scrolls sideways. The Team table scrolls inside its own
  frame.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Sparse} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, the project's name; the Details, Summary and Activity
  headings are `h2`. The breadcrumb is the "Breadcrumb" navigation, its
  last item the current page (`aria-current="page"`).
- The key facts are a list named "Key facts"; a missing PM reads
  "Unassigned" and missing dates "Not scheduled", not an empty slot.
- The aside is a `complementary` landmark named "Project summary", after
  the page in reading and focus order. The activity is a region named
  after the project ("Harbor Lights activity").
- The tab list is named "Project sections"; the Team table's caption is
  "Team", and each member's name is the row header.
- The icon-only menu button is named "More actions". The edit drawer is
  a dialog named "Edit project"; on close, focus returns to Edit. An
  empty name marks the field invalid with the message "Enter a name."

templates-object-management-projects--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProjectsStories from './Projects.stories'

<Meta of={ProjectsStories} />

# Projects

An index page, or list report: every project in saved views, narrowed by
search and filters, as a table with pages or as a chart. The table sorts,
hides columns, selects rows for a bulk archive and expands to each
project's activity. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs),
[Saved Views](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-saved-views--docs),
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs),
[Table Chart Switch](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-table-chart-switch--docs),
[Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs)'s
toolbar and footer, and the kit's Table, Column Chooser, Pagination,
BarChart, Search, Menu, Tag, Badge, Avatar and Button. The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/projects-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

From the top: the heading (title, the open count, Import, Export and the
primary action, Add project), the views, the toolbar (search, the Status and Health
filters with their chips, compact rows and Columns), the summary with the
Table / Chart switch, the table, and the footer with the pages.

## What works

- **Views** are predefined (All, Risk, On hold, Potential risk, On track,
  Archived) or saved. A view holds the filters, the columns and the sort;
  the search is not part of it. Each count is the rows the view shows
  with the current search; the view in force counts its unsaved changes
  too, so its count always matches the table.
- **Modified**: a filter, a column or a sort that differs from the view
  marks it modified. Discard puts it back; Save writes it into a saved
  view; on a predefined view, Save as new view keeps it under a new name.
  Manage views deletes saved views.
- **Search** matches the project name and the PM.
- **Filters** are checkbox menus, Status and Health; each choice shows as
  a chip that removes on its own, and Clear all removes them all.
- **Sort** by name, PM, last update, resources, timeline or estimation.
  The sort covers every page, not only the one shown.
- **Pages** of 10, 25 or 50. Any change to what is listed goes back to
  the first page.
- **Chart** shows the estimation of the same projects by status, under
  the same view, search and filters.
- **Selection** turns the toolbar into an Archive action; archived
  projects move to the Archived view. Changing the page, the view, the
  search or a filter clears it, so you never act on rows you cannot see.
- **Clear filters**, in the empty state, clears the search and puts the
  view's own filters back; it does not leave the view.
- **Expand** a row to see its activity: status changes with their note,
  estimation changes, and when it was created.
- **Import** reads a CSV of projects through the [Import
  Export](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-import-export--docs) dialog:
  the headings map to Project name, PM, Status and Estimation, an unknown
  status or an estimation that is not a number skips its row, and the
  rest join the list on track and unscheduled.
- **Export** downloads a CSV of the current view, the selected projects
  or all of them, with the columns on screen ticked; dates are ISO and
  money a bare number, for a spreadsheet to read.
- **Compact rows** switches the table to its small density, and
  **Columns** hides the ones you do not need.

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.FilterAndSaveView} />

## Make it yours

`Projects` takes `projects` (an array of `Project`, see
`projects-data.ts`) and keeps a copy in state. Replace `sampleProjects`
with your data, the `setProjects` calls (Archive) with calls to your API,
and the `views` state with the views you store per user. With many rows,
filter, sort and page on the server: the page slices locally only because
the sample is small. The activity list is the
[Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern; `ProjectActivity.tsx` turns a project's events into its
sentences, and
[Project Detail](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-project-detail--docs)
shares it.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projects` | `Project[]` | `sampleProjects` | The rows. Read once; later changes are local. |

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Tablet} />

- The sidebar sits beside the page; below 64rem it is the icon rail, and
  the header comes back with the account (App Shell).
- The heading wraps: Add project drops under the title when there is no
  room beside it.
- The toolbar wraps: on a phone the search takes its own line, and the
  filters and the table settings flow under it.
- The views scroll sideways when they do not fit, instead of wrapping
  onto a second line.
- The table keeps its columns and scrolls inside its own frame; the page
  never scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Mobile} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1` ("Projects" and the count), a `main` landmark with a skip link,
  and the sidebar as the "Main" navigation (App Shell).
- The views are a tab list named "Project views"; each tab's name
  includes its count ("Risk 3"). "Modified" is a status, announced when
  it appears (Saved Views).
- The filters are a search landmark, "Project filters"; the chips are a
  list, "Applied filters", and removing one moves focus to the next
  (Filter Bar).
- The Table / Chart switch is a second tab list, "Show projects as"; the
  count beside it ("16 projects") is a status, announced as it changes
  (Table Chart Switch).
- The table's caption names the current view ("Risk projects"); the
  project name is each row's header, so the checkbox and the expand button
  are named after it ("Select Harbor Lights", "Expand Harbor Lights").
- The pages are a navigation, "Project pages".
- An expanded row's activity is a region named after the project
  ("Harbor Lights activity"), holding an ordered list, newest first. The
  arrow between a timeline's dates is hidden and read as "to".
- A PM without a name says "Unassigned", and a project without dates says
  "Not scheduled", instead of an empty cell.
- The selection count is announced as it changes (Data Table Page).

charts-barchart.name: BarChart
charts-barchart.description: Amounts per bucket or category, stacked or grouped, with a tooltip and a table view. The y axis always starts at zero.

reactDocgen.description: Amounts per bucket or category, stacked or grouped, with a tooltip and a table view. The y axis always starts at zero.

title.description: Shown above the chart, and its accessible name.

data.description: Flat rows, one per bucket: `{ time, ok: 120, error: 4 }`. A missing or null value is a gap, not a zero.

x.description: The field holding each row's x value. Dates give a time axis, strings a category axis.

height.description: Height of the plot in pixels. The width follows the container.

format.description: Formats values on the axis, legend, tooltip and table. Defaults to compact numbers ("3.15K").

timeZone.description:
The time axis is in the viewer's time zone, or UTC. ponytail: no other named
zones, since d3 ticks only on local or UTC hours; add one when a product needs it.

isIncomplete.description: The last bucket is still filling: drawn dashed (line) or faded (bar).

legendValue.description: What the legend shows beside each series: its sum, or its latest value (for rates and latencies, where a sum means nothing).

layout.description: `stacked` adds series into one bar per bucket; `grouped` puts them side by side.

stories.name: Stacked
stories.snippet:
const Stacked = () => <BarChart
    title="Requests by status code"
    data={statusCodes}
    x="time"
    timeZone="UTC"
    isIncomplete
    series={[
      { key: 'ok', label: '2xx', color: 'success' },
      { key: 'redirect', label: '3xx', color: 'info' },
      { key: 'clientError', label: '4xx', color: 'warning' },
      { key: 'serverError', label: '5xx', color: 'danger' },
    ]} />;
stories.description: Stacked over time, in status colours. The last bucket is faded: it is still filling.
